articles.title: Anthony Vetro: From Video Coding Lab to Global R&D Leader At MERL
articles.summary:
The trajectory from researcher to top executive at a leading R&D organization doesn’t happen overnight. It took Anthony Vetro nearly 30 years to climb the corporate ladder at Mitsubishi Electric Research Laboratories, in Cambridge, Mass. He joined MERL in 1996, right out of college, and he has worked there ever since.
Vetro probably is best known for his research in multimedia signal processing, focusing on video compression.
Anthony Vetro
Employer
Mitsubishi Electric Research Laboratories, in Cambridge, Mass.
Title
Member grade
Fellow
Alma mater
Polytechnic Institute of Brooklyn (now New York University’s Tandon engineering school)
He became an IEEE Fellow in 2011 for his contributions to video coding, three-dimensional television, and multimedia adaptation.
Mitsubishi Electric has moved away from making televisions. It now focuses on developing systems including ones used for defense, electronics, the energy industry, and space exploration.
His ascension up the executive ranks began in 2018, when he was named a vice president and director of MERL. In 2023 he was appointed its president and CEO.
He also works closely with the company’s new U.S.-based innovation facility in Cambridge. And he recently took on a dual role as deputy head of Mitsubishi Electric’s global R&D activities, including in Asia and Europe.

articles.title: Peninsula Energy Halts Trading After Cyber Incident Hits US Uranium Mine
articles.summary:
Australian uranium company Peninsula Energy (ASX: PEN; OTCQB: PENMF) has requested a trading halt after a cybersecurity incident hit its uranium mine in the United States.
The incident, the company told the Australian Securities Exchange (ASX), occurred on Friday night and impacted the Lance Project in Wyoming, US.
“The company is undertaking a preliminary investigation of the incident and an assessment of the timing and impact, which will temporarily affect its operations,” Peninsula Energy said in a Monday filing.
According to the filing, the incident resulted in a breach of its “operating system”, while administrative systems in the US and Australia were not affected. It did not specify which technical systems were compromised or whether uranium production had been interrupted.
“Peninsula wishes the trading halt to remain in place until the earlier of the commencement of normal trading on 25 November 2026 or when the company releases the announcement regarding the cybersecurity incident,” the company said.
The wholly owned Lance Project, located in Crook County, relies on in situ recovery to extract uranium, which is then processed into yellowcake, which can be turned into nuclear fuel.
In 2025, the US added uranium to the federal list of critical minerals, and the Lance Project, which is expected to become a key supplier, has likely become an attractive target for hacking groups.

articles.title: ¿Qué pasa en una casa inteligente cuando se cae internet?
articles.summary:
¿Qué pasa en una casa inteligente cuando se cae internet?
Una avería en la fibra no tiene por qué dejar fuera de juego toda la domótica, pero sí puede impedir controlar luces, cámaras o electrodomésticos
Televisores, altavoces inteligentes, termostatos, cámaras de vigilancia, electrodomésticos… Cada vez utilizamos más dispositivos conectados y pocas veces nos paramos a pensar qué pasaría en caso de producirse un fallo con la conexión a internet. ¿Seguirían funcionando como si nada? ¿Podríamos controlarlos de alguna manera? Lo cierto es que no hay una respuesta universal, y al final todo depende del producto concreto y del tipo de conexión que se use para configurarlos en la red doméstica.
Lo primero que hay que tener en cuenta es que, aunque a menudo hablamos de internet (o la conexión) y del Wi-Fi como sinónimos, la realidad es que no son lo mismo: internet es la red global que permite acceder a páginas web, plataformas y servidores externos, mientras Wi-Fi es la tecnología que conecta nuestros dispositivos con la red local del hogar sin cables. ¿Por qué es importante esta diferencia? Porque una avería en la conexión de fibra óptica puede dejarnos sin acceso a internet, pero si el router sigue encendido y funcionando, la red doméstica puede seguir comunicando los dispositivos entre sí, siempre que estos dispongan de una vía de comunicación local. En cambio, si el router deja de funcionar, los dispositivos que dependen de él para comunicarse pueden perder esa conexión, aunque…

articles.summary:
Google quiere limitar el poder de los agentes de IA dentro de Chrome. La compañía propone un sistema de permisos a nivel de navegador para controlar qué webs pueden visitar y qué acciones pueden realizar. La iniciativa surge tras la oleada de incidentes en donde los agentes se han saltado las barreras de seguridad y terminan hackeando páginas o accediendo a contenido para el que no estaban autorizados.
De acuerdo con Neowin, Google ha planeado un sistema que limitaría el alcance de los agentes autónomos. Ingenieros de la empresa propusieron cambios en WebDriver BiDi, el protocolo utilizado para automatización y pruebas en navegadores. En una publicación en el grupo de Chromium, los empleados anunciaron una intención para prototipar la idea y regresarle el control a los usuarios.
En la versión actual del protocolo, WebDriver BiDi asume una relación de confianza total entre el cliente y el navegador, lo que permite un control prácticamente ilimitado. Si bien esto funciona para pruebas automatizadas, resulta peligroso para agentes de IA que navegan en la web. Muchos agentes usan protocolos de bajo nivel o configuraciones que les dan acceso sin restricciones y sin supervisión del usuario.

articles.title: Der KI-Masterplan ist veraltet, bevor er beschlossen wird – was Unternehmen stattdessen tun sollten
articles.summary:
Der KI-Masterplan ist veraltet, bevor er beschlossen wird – was Unternehmen stattdessen tun sollten
Mitte September hat der Bitkom neue Zahlen veröffentlicht. 57 Prozent der Unternehmen in Deutschland setzen inzwischen KI ein, ein Jahr zuvor waren es 36 Prozent. Mich haben zwei andere Zahlen aus derselben Befragung mehr beschäftigt. 66 Prozent aller befragten Unternehmen schätzen die KI-Kompetenz ihrer Beschäftigten als gering ein. Und nur elf Prozent schulen alle Beschäftigten im Umgang mit KI.
Die Lizenzen sind also schnell gekauft. Was danach kommen soll, ist in vielen Organisationen offen. Wie führt man ein Unternehmen dahin, KI sinnvoll zu verankern, wenn niemand weiß, wie das Ziel genau aussieht?
Der Plan ist auch eine Absicherung
Die naheliegende Antwort ist ein Masterplan. Drei Jahre, klare Meilensteine, ein Budget, das hält. Im ersten Schritt ist das nachvollziehbar. Aufsichtsrat und Banken wollen wissen, wofür Geld ausgegeben wird, und Mitarbeitende wollen wissen, woran sie sind. Ein Plan schützt außerdem den, der ihn geschrieben hat. Geht etwas schief, hat man sich zumindest an den Plan gehalten.
Bei KI ändert sich die Grundlage jeder Planung allerdings in Monaten. Modelle werden leistungsfähiger, Preise und Nutzungsbedingungen verschieben sich, neue Werkzeuge sind da, bevor die alten eingeführt sind. Viele etablierte Geschäftsmodelle stehen unter Druck und neue Geschäftsmodelle implodieren genauso schnell, wie sie entstanden sind. Und manchmal ist ein Werkzeug übe…

articles.title: El Niño e aquecimento global levam temperatura da Terra a novo recorde
articles.summary:
A Terra registrou o dia com a maior anomalia de temperatura já medida: na sexta-feira (20), a temperatura média global ficou 2,12 °C acima dos níveis pré-industriais. Os dados preliminares são do Serviço de Mudanças Climáticas Copernicus (C3S), da Europa, e representam novo alerta sobre a intensidade do aquecimento do planeta.
O recorde é resultado da combinação entre as mudanças climáticas provocadas pela atividade humana e um episódio excepcionalmente forte do fenômeno El Niño. O evento atual pode ser o mais intenso dos últimos mil anos.
O fenômeno ainda está ganhando força e deve atingir seu ápice aproximadamente no próximo mês. Por isso, cientistas esperam que novos dias com temperaturas pelo menos 2 °C acima da média pré-industrial sejam registrados nos próximos meses.
El Niño pode provocar novos recordes de temperatura
- A influência do El Niño sobre a temperatura global não acontece de maneira instantânea. O calor liberado no Oceano Pacífico leva algum tempo para afetar as médias de temperatura do planeta, o que significa que os efeitos mais intensos do fenômeno ainda podem estar por vir;
- Zachary Labe, cientista da organização de pesquisa climática Climate Central, acredita que novas marcas podem aparecer em breve.

articles.title: Elecbrakes Bluetooth Vulnerabilities Expose Trailers to Forced Braking
articles.summary:
Vulnerabilities discovered in Bluetooth-enabled brake controllers made by Australian firm Elecbrakes could allow hackers to manipulate trailer brakes, potentially causing accidents, researchers warned.
The affected products include the EB2, VM1 and ELBC 2000 brake controllers from Elecbrakes. According to the cybersecurity agency CISA, which last week published an advisory on the vulnerabilities, the affected brake controllers are mainly used in Australia and New Zealand.
The controllers regulate the braking force applied to trailers, with the EB2 unit mounted on the trailer and the VM1 unit on the towing vehicle. The devices can be controlled remotely via a special remote or a smartphone app.
Researchers from Australian IT and cybersecurity consultancy Element Digital — with help from AI — discovered three vulnerabilities in the braking controllers, including two critical missing authentication and insufficient replay-attack protection issues.
They demonstrated that an unauthenticated attacker who is within Bluetooth range of the targeted vehicle (up to 100 meters or 328 feet) can use a laptop or phone to engage or release a trailer’s brakes or adjust the braking force, without any interaction required from the victim.
“Your trailer’s brakes slamming to maximum while your tow vehicle keeps going is the exact recipe for a jackknife – one of the more reliably fatal things a vehicle combination can do,” the researchers warned.

articles.title: A tiny supercurrent could unlock quantum information without destroying it
articles.summary:
A tiny supercurrent could unlock quantum information without destroying it
Scientists have developed a promising new method that could read quantum information with 99.85% accuracy while barely disturbing the qubit itself.
- Date:
  November 4, 2026
- Source:
  Fundação de Amparo à Pesquisa do Estado de São Paulo
- Summary:
  Researchers have proposed a breakthrough technique for reading quantum information without destroying the delicate states that make quantum computers work. By detecting an electrical signal generated by the qubit itself, their method achieved up to 99.85% accuracy in simulations and could make future quantum computers simpler and more efficient.
- Share:
One of the biggest obstacles in quantum computing is surprisingly simple to describe: how do you read information without changing or destroying it? Unlike the bits used in ordinary computers, quantum bits, or qubits, are extraordinarily sensitive to measurement. Trying to determine their state can cause that state to collapse, potentially erasing the very information scientists want to retrieve.
Researchers have now proposed a way to overcome much of this difficulty by using an unusual electrical signal produced by the qubit itself. Their approach focuses on a special type known as an "Andreev qubit," which can generate an oscillating electric supercurrent through its own quantum behavior. By monitoring this current, scientists may be able to determine the qubit's state without directly measuring it or …

articles.summary:
Validate UCIe.mem implementations across development stages while reusing a common verification environment.
By Ujjwal Negi and Prashant Dixit
As chiplet-based designs become increasingly common, connecting compute and memory dies efficiently is an important part of building scalable systems. The Universal Chiplet Interconnect Express (UCIe) standard provides a common die-to-die interconnect, while UCIe.mem defines a standardized protocol for memory transactions between compute and memory chiplets.
Modern systems can combine compute chiplets with different memory technologies, including HBM, DDR, and LPDDR. Traditionally, integrating these components can involve technology-specific interfaces and custom mechanisms. UCIe.mem addresses the growing need for scalable and flexible memory architectures in modern computing systems by providing a common, memory-technology-agnostic way to communicate memory requests and responses across chiplets.
This standardization provides a foundation for more modular and scalable chiplet-based architectures. It allows compute and memory chiplets to be developed independently and integrated across implementations from different vendors, reducing reliance on custom, technology-specific interfaces. By decoupling memory communication from the underlying memory technology, UCIe.mem gives system designers greater flexibility to combine, reuse, and scale compute and memory resources to meet different application requirements.

Neural networks can learn patterns from these histories across instruments and forecast horizons.
NVIDIA Megatron Core is an open-source library of GPU-optimized components for training transformer models at scale. articles.summary:
A hidden limit of space and time could unlock electronics 100,000 times faster
- Date:
  November 7, 2026
- Source:
  University of Regensburg
- Summary:
  Scientists have discovered a surprising quantum limit that prevents electrons from being tracked with unlimited precision in both space and time. The breakthrough could pave the way for manipulating chemical reactions and developing electronics hundreds of thousands of times faster than today's technology.
- Share:
Quantum physics places fundamental limits on what scientists can know about the behavior of particles. Werner Heisenberg's famous uncertainty principle states that certain properties, such as a particle's position and momentum, cannot both be measured with unlimited precision. This restriction is not caused by flaws in scientific instruments. It is built into the laws of nature.
But position and time are different. Heisenberg's uncertainty principle does not impose the same restriction on these quantities. Now, researchers have experimentally demonstrated another fundamental limitation: an electron's location and its behavior over time cannot both be determined with arbitrary precision. Known as the "space-time limit," this newly observed relationship could have major implications for the future of quantum technology and ultrafast electronics.

Plusieurs victimes ont été recensées en France ces derniers jours, avec des montants dérobés allant de 500 à plus de 1 000 euros. Il faut dire que cette arnaque est difficilement repérable. Une victime peut effectuer un paiement ou retirer de l’argent en saisissant son code PIN, sans rien remarquer. Cependant, un point précis peut alerter sur la situation.
Une minuscule caméra et un lecteur de carte piégé pour vider vos comptes bancaires
Une nouvelle arnaque, particulièrement élaborée, a été repérée à plusieurs reprises ces derniers jours en France. Cette arnaque vise plus particulièrement les stations-service et les distributeurs de billets. En d’autres termes, tous les dispositifs qui demandent d’insérer une carte bancaire et de saisir un code PIN. Le mode de fonctionnement de cette arnaque est, il faut le dire, sophistiqué. Comme l’explique BFMTV, les arnaqueurs parviennent à intégrer un dispositif dans le lecteur de carte d’un système de paiement. Ce dispositif est ensuite capable d’intercepter les données échangées avec la puce de la carte bancaire. Il est ici plus précisément question de skimming, une technique qui consiste à insérer un boîtier très fin dans le lecteur afin de récupérer les données de la carte.

articles.title: New Shirudo tool uses AI to shield unpatched Linux systems from exploits
articles.summary:
OpenAI and Cisco launched an open-source Linux security tool named Shirudo that deploys temporary runtime protections to block vulnerability exploitation while administrators prepare and roll out patches, without restarting services.
Shirudo leverages the eBPF (extended Berkeley Packet Filter) mechanism in Linux to monitor for suspicious activity and deploy targeted protections called "shields."
eBPF is a Linux technology that lets programs run in a controlled environment within the operating system's kernel without modifying its source code or requiring a restart.
It enables real-time monitoring of system and network activity, performance analysis, and enforcement of targeted security protections, making it an ideal operational basis for Shirudo.
Shirudo’s shields aim to block malicious behavior in a targeted way, leaving legitimate application operations undisturbed. OpenAI highlights four core capabilities for the tool:
- Live protection: Blocks vulnerable code paths without restarting systems, letting operators assess shield impact before enforcing them.
- AI-assisted defense: Enables agents to investigate vulnerabilities, develop shields, and validate their effectiveness, with deployment remaining under human control.
- Trusted deployment: Uses cryptographic signatures, Linux's eBPF verifier, and kernel security controls to prevent unauthorized modifications.

Now Firefox can select which sites use its VPN, and clear your browsing history with one click

articles.title: Huang reportedly admitted to more than two affairs to Nvidia's board
articles.summary:
In a complete U-turn, Nvidia’s board on Monday reinstated Jensen Huang as the CEO and president of the chipmaker, just a fortnight after he resigned.
During a meeting before his reinstatement, however, Huang admitted to more affairs beyond the two that have been reported in the news, according to The Wall Street Journal.
Early in November, Huang admitted to an extramarital affair in a letter to employees. At the time, he was ostensibly talking about his relationship with Megaspeed executive and alleged Chinese spy, Alice Huang (not related to Jensen). Later, it was reported that he’d also had a relationship with Nvidia’s VP of health, Kimberly Powell.
Afterwards, Reuters reported that he also had an affair with another employee.
It’s not clear which affairs Huang admitted to during this recent conversation with Nvidia’s board of directors.
Huang’s return was spurred by a personal intervention from the U.S. government, Nvidia’s board said in a statement on Monday, and President Donald Trump apparently called the board to bat for Huang’s reinstatement.
The Wall Street Journal reports that over the weekend, U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche told Trump and Vice President JD Vance that the Justice Department wasn’t investigating Huang and there was no evidence that he was a national security risk, after which both contacted the company’s board.
Huang received a “hero’s welcome” at Nvidia’s HQ, with several employees applauding his return.

articles.title: OpenAI, Cisco Unveil Open Source Tool to Shield Unpatched Linux Systems

OpenAI and Cisco on Monday unveiled Shirudo, an open source security platform that uses AI agents to prevent the exploitation of vulnerabilities in Linux systems and applications.
The project is an AI-focused rewrite of Cisco-owned Isovalent’s Tetragon runtime security platform. Tetragon was open-sourced in 2022, and it also powers Cisco’s Live Protect vulnerability mitigation technology.
Shirudo is designed to help defenders address the challenges introduced by AI-accelerated vulnerability discovery and exploitation, which is increasing pressure on organizations to deploy patches quickly.
The tool leverages eBPF technology to modify Linux kernel behavior without restarting the OS.
According to Cisco and OpenAI, agents can analyze vulnerability information, generate so-called ‘shields’ to prevent exploitation, and test their effectiveness without disrupting important services. Security teams still retain control over which shields are deployed.
Protections are digitally signed and verified before deployment, with mechanisms designed to prevent even attackers with root privileges from disabling kernel-level enforcement.
In a controlled test targeting the recent Java4Shell vulnerability, a shield generated using OpenAI’s Codex blocked an exploitation attempt targeting an Elasticsearch instance without requiring a restart.

Desde allí es posible consultar los dispositivos activos, ver su nombre, el tipo de aparato y, en algunos casos, controlar cuánto tiempo pueden permanecer conectados.
Antes de bloquear un equipo, conviene identificar los aparatos propios. Un teléfono puede aparecer con un nombre técnico, mientras que una consola, una impresora o un televisor suelen figurar con la marca del fabricante. articles.title: McDonald's Japan data breach exposes customer location information
articles.summary:
McDonald's Japan, the fast-food giant's Japanese subsidiary, has disclosed a data breach after attackers accessed a database containing sensitive information for users of the company's official smartphone app.
Founded in 1940, McDonald's is now a multinational fast-food chain that operates more than 40,000 restaurants in more than 100 countries and serves tens of millions of customers daily.
In a Friday statement, the company's Japanese subsidiary confirmed that threat actors gained access to its official app's database and said the exposed information includes the users' product purchase history, IP addresses, mobile device location data, and customer management IDs (which cannot be used to identify the customers' email addresses or member IDs).
McDonald's Japan also added that the exposed data doesn't include the affected customers' names, email addresses, phone numbers, home addresses, or credit card information.
While it has yet to reveal when it detected the attack or how many individuals had their data stolen, the company said a follow-up investigation found no service disruption or misuse of official apps as a result of the incident.
"We are working to invalidate any credentials used for unauthorized access, investigate the relevant systems, and report to the Personal Information Protection Commission," it said. "In addition, we will strive to strengthen security measures and prevent recurrence."

articles.title: Auchan, Leclerc, Lidl : pourquoi ces pommes de terre sont devenues naturellement toxiques
articles.summary:
Quand un légume est rappelé, on soupçonne d’habitude un résidu de pesticide ou une bactérie. Ici, c’est le tubercule lui-même qui pose problème. Comme le rapporte franceinfo, plusieurs fiches de rappel publiées entre le samedi 21 et ce mardi 24 novembre 2026 visent des pommes de terre rouges trop riches en glycoalcaloïdes, vendues chez Auchan, E.Leclerc et Lidl.
Les trois rappels portent sur le même numéro de lot, 26128774. La fiche RappelConso publiée par Leclerc ce lundi 23 novembre prévient que ces substances peuvent provoquer « nausées, maux de ventre, vomissements et diarrhées ».
Pourquoi une pomme de terre devient-elle toxique ?
La pomme de terre fait partie des solanacées, comme la tomate et l’aubergine. D’après Santé Canada, ces plantes produisent des glycoalcaloïdes, surtout l’alpha-solanine et l’alpha-chaconine, sans doute pour se défendre contre les insectes, les champignons et les bactéries. À faible dose, ces molécules donnent même son goût au tubercule. Mais leur taux grimpe quand la pomme de terre verdit à la lumière, germe ou s’abîme.
En 2020, l’Autorité européenne de sécurité des aliments (EFSA) a fixé la plus petite dose aux effets nocifs observés à 1 milligramme par kilo de poids corporel et par jour, soit 70 milligrammes pour un adulte de 70 kilos. Les nourrissons et les jeunes enfants, plus légers, sont donc les plus exposés. L’épluchage aide, car selon l’EFSA, il réduit la teneur de 25 à 75 %.

articles.title: Anthropic Expands Enterprise Safeguards for Detecting AI Misuse

Anthropic on Monday announced the public beta of Enterprise Frontier Safeguards (EFS), a system designed to help organizations detect malicious use of AI.
Unveiled in September, EFS has been developed with input from over 100 Anthropic customers, with companies such as Stripe and Salesforce evaluating it in private beta. A quarter of Fortune 100 companies helped develop EFS.
According to Anthropic, existing Claude protections can identify potentially harmful requests made individually, but EFS adds a monitoring layer that can detect suspicious patterns across multiple requests that may appear benign when analyzed individually.
The system targets organizations that use Claude under zero data retention agreements and have so far relied only on classifiers that analyze each request in isolation.
EFS is designed to detect both deliberate misuse of AI, such as AI-powered cyberattacks, and incidents where AI agents go beyond what their operator intended, such as the cases where agents exploited vulnerabilities to gain access to real-world systems.
With EFS, organizations store conversation data in their own cloud and protect it with their own encryption keys and access policies.
Neither Anthropic nor its cloud providers retain copies of the conversation data after it’s transferred to the customer’s storage. Anthropic receives monitoring metadata, but not the content of conversations.

articles.title: A Link Is Not Architecture: Why Multi-Die Systems Need More Than Die-to-Die Connectivity
articles.summary:
Maintaining consistent communication behavior, integration, and security across configurations.
The system-on-chip (SoC) transformed semiconductor design by bringing the major functions of an electronic system onto one die, an integration that shaped chip architecture for years. Multi-die design is now changing the model again, distributing system functionality across multiple dies within a single package.
While this approach gives engineers greater flexibility to align semiconductor design with system requirements, bringing these designs to life takes more than a die-to-die link to transport transactions across the package. It requires a system architecture that manages how data moves between dies.
In AI and high-performance computing (HPC) systems, multi-die architectures enable teams to scale compute and select an appropriate process technology for each part of the design. These partitioning choices determine which transactions remain within a die and which must cross die boundaries. Treating each boundary independently increases integration and verification effort, complicates performance management, and reduces the practical value of chiplet reuse.
Still, managing communication across these die boundaries requires a clear separation between the physical interface that transports transactions and the system architecture that manages them. En 1930 se cazó el último lince boreal en libertad del que hay constancia en Cataluña, y su piel acabó expuesta en la comarca del Ripollès, tal y como recoge la Fundación para la Conservación del Quebrantahuesos. Casi un siglo después, dos asociaciones ecologistas plantearon en octubre de 2025 devolver este felino al Pirineo catalán con una prueba piloto que todavía está lejos de convertirse en realidad.

articles.title: From Vulnerability Noise to Resilience: Rethinking Security in the AI Era
articles.summary:
Written by: George Manuelian, Chief Strategy Officer, RapidFort
The modern software stack has become an iceberg. The application code customers and security teams see at the surface is only a small portion of what is being shipped. Beneath it sit operating systems, frameworks, libraries, packages, and transitive dependencies, with much of it drawn from open source or third parties.
As AI accelerates software development, that hidden complexity has become an even more critical security challenge.
For business and technology leaders, the question is no longer simply how many vulnerabilities exist. It is where does meaningful risk live, which vulnerabilities can be exploited in our environment, and how we can reduce that risk without turning developers into full-time vulnerability managers.
The answer requires a fundamental shift from vulnerability accumulation to continuous software resilience.
First step: Recognizing composition of modern software
The typical containerized stack is layers of base operating system software, packages, libraries, language frameworks and dependencies, and the application itself. The application a company writes may represent only a small portion of what it ultimately ships.
That is important because vulnerabilities multiply. A vulnerable package in a base image is not necessarily one vulnerability in practice; it can be replicated across every application and container that uses that image.

V2G appears poised for increased adoption by automakers due to the release of a new certification program for V2G technologies based on the recently issued UL 1741 Supplement SC standard. (Note that one variation of V2G is V2H, or vehicle-to-home, but we’re focusing just on V2G here.)
This adjunct standard creates a formal testing and certification pathway for bidirectional electric vehicle supply equipment (BEVSE) under UL 1741, the primary North American safety and performance standard for inverters, converters, charge controllers, and interconnection system equipment (ISE) used in distributed energy resources (DERs), such as solar panels, wind turbines, and home battery-storage systems (Figure 2).

GreyNoise believes the threat actor has been using agentic harnesses and systems to weaponize vulnerabilities, find vulnerable assets, and automatically exploit them. The automated operations were complemented by hands-on-keyboard activity.

articles.title: Vercel will make AI providers prove they don’t keep prompts. Here’s why it matters for developers.

Vercel will make AI providers prove they don’t keep prompts. Here’s why it matters for developers.
Since April, developers using Vercel’s AI Gateway have been able to request provider-level zero data retention (ZDR). Vercel says its existing provider-level ZDR routing relies on providers’ policies and agreements with the company; the new tier adds a requirement for published independent audits.
On Monday, Vercel announced Audited ZDR, a tier that will admit providers only after independent security firms test their retention claims against their code, infrastructure, and live traffic and publish the reports. Vercel says a planned team-wide toggle will restrict routing and failover to providers with qualifying published audits. The announcement does not give a separate general-availability date for the toggle.
Vercel says launch partners Baseten, Modal, and Wafer have begun their audits, with reports expected by December 8. Each provider will enter the tier once its qualifying report is published.
The announcement follows research published November 19 by industrial cybersecurity firm Dragos, which sent about 2 million prompts containing trackable credentials and URLs to AI services. Vercel’s announcement does not cite that research. On Sunday, OpenRouter said it’d removed three providers and stripped 125 endpoints of their ZDR eligibility as a result.

articles.title: Pinterest will now let parents limit the AI-generated content their teens see
articles.summary:
Pinterest announced this week that it’s expanding its parental controls, but one new feature stands out: Parents can now control how much AI-generated content their children are exposed to. This additional setting arrives alongside more standard options, like tools to adjust notifications or whether or not videos auto-play.
The change makes Pinterest one of the first major social platforms to allow parents to control how much AI-generated content is shown to their children as part of the overall user experience.
Aside from Pinterest, social media platforms have focused more on limiting minors’ access to specific AI-powered features, as when Snap added a parental control setting that prevented its AI chatbot from responding to teens or when Meta announced a global pause on teens’ access to existing AI characters after retooling the product based on parents’ feedback.
WhatsApp currently allows parents to adjust the level of access teens have to Meta AI, in terms of using AI to create content or having the AI respond to their teen’s questions.
But when it comes to AI-generated content filling users’ feeds and recommendations, there are few controls available on social media platforms in general, much less those provided as part of the parental controls.

articles.title: The clock is running out for America’s most contentious spying law
articles.summary:
Weeks before the end of the legislative session, some members of Congress are scrambling to reauthorize a controversial warrantless wiretapping authority, possibly by attaching it to a must-pass military spending bill. Sen. Mike Rounds (R-SD) told Politicothat Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act (FISA) could be attached to the National Defense Authorization Act. It’s the latest in a grueling fight over a major spying rule that hasn’t technically lapsed.
The clock is running out for America’s most contentious spying law
Warrantless wiretapping proponents are rushing to beat the looming blue wave.
“We don’t have two weeks to work just on FISA,” said Rounds, a member of the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence. “But if it’s amended onto the NDAA then you can move it forward and get that done in time.”
FISA allows for the warrantless surveillance of certain foreigners’ communications, ostensibly on national security grounds. In part because of FISA’s broad scope, Congress revisits it every few years, both to reauthorize the authority and to reform it. The last effort to do both failed. Despite pressure from President Donald Trump, Congress failed to reauthorize FISA over the summer, in part because leadership wouldn’t allow any amendments — particularly attempts to limit its sweeping scope — to be debated or introduced. Formula 1 racing is an adrenaline-fueled contest of drivers, machines and split-second decisions. Behind the spectacle is an equally intense engineering competition built on data simulations, advanced modeling and constant testing.

Federal CTO at Intel.

La canela fue la quinta especia más importada por la UE en 2023. También ha sufrido un control de laboratorio. Los laboratorios de Europa han puesto a prueba a esta especia. El Centro Común de Investigación (JRC) ha analizado 104 productos de venta. De ellos, un 66,3 % tenían algún problema.
Entre ellos se detectaron problemas de calidad o incumplimientos de seguridad alimentaria. En algunos se sospechaba de fraude y en otros había un posible riesgo asociado a su contenido en cumarina. Sin embargo, esto no quiere decir que dos tercios de la canela que se comercializa en Europa tenga estos problemas.
Los problemas pueden ser muy diversos. Desde los que implican un incumplimiento de los estándares internacionales de calidad hasta posibles sospechas de adulteración o dudas en cuanto a la seguridad alimentaria. Esto último no implica que haya un fraude demostrado o que sean necesariamente peligrosos para el consumidor.
Ya se habían dado casos preocupantes. En el año 2021 se publicó un informe europeo donde se detectaron indicios de adulteración en algunas especias. Así ocurrió con pimienta, comino, cúrcuma, azafrán o pimentón. En el caso de la canela, la Comisión ha hecho públicos los resultados el 24 de septiembre de 2025. Las muestras fueron adquiridas en 10 países de la UE.

articles.title: Altersvorsorgedepot: Banken werben schon, der Staat lässt wohl auf sich warten
articles.summary:
Altersvorsorgedepot: Banken legen los – doch der Staat verspätet sich
Während sich Banken und Versicherer schon eine Werbeschlacht um das neue Altersvorsorgedepot liefern, werden Verbraucher noch länger auf die staatliche Variante warten müssen. Eigentlich sieht die neue Form der staatlich geförderten privaten Altersvorsorge vor, dass nicht nur Broker und Banken das neue Produkt anbieten. Auch der Staat sollte ein Altersvorsorgedepot auflegen.
Wie das Redaktionsnetzwerk Deutschland (RND) berichtet, wird das staatliche Depot aber zum Start am 1. Januar nicht zur Verfügung stehen. Aus Regierungskreisen heißt es, mit der Einführung sei frühestens im Sommer 2027 zu rechnen. Grund für die Verzögerung ist, dass die Verordnung für das öffentlich organisierte Angebot länger dauert als gedacht.
Die Rechtsverordnung muss auch noch festlegen, welche Institution das Angebot verwalten soll. Im Gespräch sind unter anderem Bundesbank, KfW und Deutsche Rentenversicherung. Das Gesetz zum Altersvorsorgedepot ist seit Ende Mai in Kraft.
Das Altersvorsorgedepot ist der Nachfolger der Riester-Rente und soll es den Deutschen leichter machen, breit gestreut am Kapitalmarkt fürs Alter zu sparen. Dafür gibt es staatliche Zuschüsse von bis zu 540 Euro pro Jahr sowie zusätzlich 300 Euro jährlich je kindergeldberechtigtem Kind. Anlegen können Sparer:innen in ETFs, Aktienfonds und Anleihen.

articles.title: 1 600 sorties en une semaine : Steam peine à suivre et les délais de validation explosent
articles.summary:
Pour vendre un jeu sur Steam, un studio doit passer par Steamworks, l’espace que Valve réserve aux développeurs. Il y fait vérifier son compte (identité et informations fiscales), puis Valve examine sa page boutique et son jeu.
Jusqu’ici, ces étapes prenaient quelques jours, tout au plus deux semaines. Mais ce mardi 24 novembre, le développeur indépendant derrière Murder Meet Cute a alerté sur Bluesky : d’après d’autres développeurs, ces délais atteignent désormais 45 jours.
Autrement dit, un studio qui ouvre son compte cette semaine ne pourra pas montrer son jeu sur Steam avant janvier, voire fin janvier si ces 45 jours sont des jours ouvrés, comme l’évoquent plusieurs témoignages.
Le Black Friday est lancé sur l’univers Apple. Sur Back Market, profitez de promotions sur les iPhone, MacBook, iPad, AirPods et Apple Watch. Chaque appareil est soumis à jusqu’à 100 points de contrôle qualité et est livré avec une garantie de 12 mois. De quoi profiter de performances comparables à celles d’un produit neuf.
Une avalanche de jeux
Début novembre, ce même développeur parlait déjà de délais passés de 15 à 30 jours pour valider un compte. Il conseillait alors aux autres studios de « planifier en conséquence ». Il accompagnait son analyse du graphe des sorties sur Steam au fil des semaines.
On peut voir une moyenne de 400 jeux par semaine tout au long des années 2024 et 2025, avant une explosion en 2026 jusqu’à 1600 sorties par semaine.

articles.title: How Can AI Build Faster And Better Silicon For Physical AI?
articles.summary:
Shortening the path from design intent to verified implementation could put custom silicon within reach of more teams.
The age of physical AI is here, and with it comes a significant increase in the demand of custom silicon.
By 2025, five million industrial robots were operating worldwide. As these systems become more capable, their demands on silicon become more distinct. Each must balance computation and memory with the realities of power, latency, reliability, and security.
Fig. 1: Annual installations of industrial robots, 5 largest markets, 2025. Source: International Federation of Robotics, World Robotics 2026. Chart redrawn by ChipAgents.
For humanoid robots in particular, application-specific hardware can provide the agility and speed required to perform specialized tasks in real time. As those requirements diverge, specialized ASICs become more attractive, because they can be optimized for the exact workloads, latency targets, power envelopes, and operating environments of a particular system.
The constraint to this innovation is development speed: AI models and software evolve faster than the conventional silicon tape out cycles, creating a need to accelerate the entire path from design intent and exploration to physical implementation and validation.
For agentic AI to deliver that acceleration, it must meet three requirements.

articles.summary:
In 1714, the British Parliament offered up to 20,000 pounds, a fortune at the time (roughly $3.5 million in today’s Canadian dollars), for a reliable way to determine longitude at sea—a problem that was costing sailors their lives. The answer didn’t come from astronomers of the day; it was John Harrison, a self-taught carpenter and clockmaker, who developed the marine chronometer and made ocean navigation safer.
What could a prize like that help Canadian innovators solve today?
“Canada can’t grow the innovation economy with public money and regulation. It’s stifling, overly restrictive, and full of red tape.”
Fiona Simpson, BioMimir
Robert Kaul, CEO of remote patient monitoring company Cloud DX, would like to find out. In a MaRS pulse-check of 21 high-growth founders and executives looking at what it takes to scale a company in Canada, Kaul proposed putting up $100 million to incentivize startups to solve “the hardest problems the country faces,” from hospital overcrowding and lagging productivity to homelessness and substance addiction.

Toronto-based MaRS Discovery District is marking 25 years as the anchor innovation hub for Canadian startups. articles.title: Why a Crusoe investor is betting on solar and batteries to power future AI data centers
articles.summary:
The problem of supplying power to AI data centers has become one of the central debates of the AI era. In just a few years, the U.S. grid has gone from basically zero growth to adding several gigawatts a year.
“Demand is growing faster than people appreciate,” Brook Porter, partner at G2 Venture Partners (G2VP), told TechCrunch. “It’s atoms, not bits, and the world is in the process of recognizing the realities of those challenges.”
It’s been a bumpy road. Because it takes a while to scale supply chains, companies have been securing power in any form they can. In many cases, that has meant buying, renting, and deploying natural gas power plants, but Porter thinks that hyperscalers and data center developers should look at the bigger picture if they want to move faster.
That picture involves solar paired with energy storage, based on an analysis Porter and his colleagues at G2VP recently conducted on the state of the data center power market.
“Global capacity of natural gas is only about 60 or 70 gigawatts per year, where solar is already at well over a terawatt,” he said. “Probably the most important lesson that we’ve learned over the last 20 years of backing companies is that Wright’s Law is the thing you want to leverage — making the same thing over and over again.”

articles.summary:
A Huawei foi considerada culpada de conspiração para roubar segredos comerciais e de fraude bancária em um julgamento realizado nos Estados Unidos. Por outro lado, a gigante chinesa de tecnologia e telecomunicações foi absolvida da acusação mais abrangente de associação criminosa, considerada mais grave no processo. O veredicto foi divulgado nesta terça-feira (24), após dois meses de julgamento.O julgamento durou dois meses, e as acusações contra a companhia foram anunciadas pela primeira vez por promotores federais em 2019.
Durante o processo, os promotores acusaram a empresa de recorrer a mentiras, fraudes e roubo de informações para obter vantagens competitivas no mercado. A defesa da Huawei contestou a abordagem da acusação e afirmou que os investigadores partiram da premissa de que a companhia era uma organização criminosa, construindo o caso a partir dessa interpretação. As informações são da BBC.
Huawei se manifesta após veredicto
Em sua defesa, a empresa argumentou que seu sucesso comercial foi resultado de inovação própria, e não de práticas criminosas. A estratégia dos advogados foi questionar a maneira como o caso foi conduzido pelos promotores norte-americanos.
Após a decisão, a Huawei divulgou um comunicado no qual destacou a absolvição da acusação de associação criminosa. Segundo a companhia, o resultado confirma que as alegações relacionadas a esse ponto não tinham fundamento factual.

articles.title: Mozilla explica por que não há um Firefox "puro" para iPhone
articles.summary:
Mozilla explica por que não há um Firefox “puro” para iPhone
Mozilla afirma que regras impostas pela Apple são complexas e inviabilizam o Firefox de ter seu próprio motor no iOS.
A Mozilla lançou a primeira versão do Firefox para iPhone em 2015. Mas, até hoje, o navegador não conta com uma implementação totalmente “pura” no iOS, com motor próprio. Em tom de desabafo, a organização explicou o motivo. Saiba desde já que, sim, a Mozilla culpa a Apple por isso.
Quando falamos de motor, nos referimos ao componente central do navegador, que interpreta o código de páginas web escrito em padrões como HTML, CSS e JavaScript, e transforma esse conjunto de informações em um conteúdo visual e interativo para o usuário.
Hoje, a maior parte dos navegadores é baseada no projeto Chromium, a exemplo do Microsoft Edge, do Opera, do Brave e, claro, do Google Chrome. No Chromium, o motor utilizado é o Blink.
O Firefox é diferente, pois conta com um motor próprio: o Gecko. Mas, no iOS, o navegador é executado a partir do WebKit, motor mantido pela Apple que, como tal, é a base do Safari.
É aqui que está o ponto de conflito: se dependesse da Mozilla, o Firefox também contaria com o Gecko no iPhone.
A Apple exigia que os navegadores para iOS usassem o WebKit sob o argumento de que essa condição favorecia aspectos como segurança, privacidade e desempenho. Isso mudou em 2024, quando a Digital Markets Act (DMA) passou a vigorar. Trata-se de uma legislação da União Europeia que busca aumentar a concorr…

Through the looking glass: Companies that have invested millions or billions into AI aren't being discouraged by the "slop" label. Google, for example, has filed a patent application for an entirely AI-generated TV channel in which the main character is... you. If that doesn't sound off-putting enough, the content will be based on the data Google collects about you, and it will also feature customized ads.
First noticed by Patentlyze, Google's AI-generated channel, imaginatively called "My Channel," is described as an option in a TV app. The content it generates will be based on demographic data, device data, YouTube watch history, and any other information Google holds about the user, who will also be the protagonist in these shows.
Once someone clicks on the channel, they will be given options to watch a personalized show starring themselves. Examples include sci-fi adventures, fun romantic comedies, and an action/thriller experience, all featuring the user's own likeness and voice. These shows can be created with or without specific user requests.
One section describes how, if a person watched a lot of sports videos, such as the best moments of a particular player, the system could create a video of the player's highlights interspersed with footage of the user cheering in the stands. The user could even be shown "interacting" with the player – something that sounds a little concerning.

articles.title: Adyen’s co-founder Pieter van der Does to retire as Co-CEO; Ingo Uytdehaage to become sole CEO
articles.summary:
Pieter van der Does, co-founder and Co-CEO of Dutch Fintech Adyen, is stepping down from his executive role after 20 years at the helm of one of Europe’s most prominent technology companies.
In an announcement on 23 November 2026, marking Adyen’s 20th anniversary, the company said van der Does will retire on 31 December 2026, and Ingo Uytdehaage, Co-CEO since 2023, will become sole CEO
“After 20 years, this is the right moment for me to step down on a positive note and with a very good feeling. Adyen has been my life’s work, and I’m incredibly proud of what our teams and customers have built together over the past two decades. Ingo and I have worked very closely together as Co-CEOs, and now we have completed the transition,” said van der Does, co-founder and co-CEO of Adyen.
Arnout Schuijff and van der Does launched Adyen in 2006, and the company was formally incorporated on 23 November 2006, when Schuijff visited a notary in Amsterdam to formally establish the company. Van der Does, who was on a sabbatical in Brazil at the time, followed the proceedings remotely over Skype.
Before starting Adyen, the co-founders had previously worked together at payments company Bibit, and their shared ambition became Adyen, which means “doing it again” in Surinamese. In his farewell letter, Van der Does says, “Adyen outgrew our wildest imagination.”

La herramienta puede combinar elementos de distintas imágenes para proponer una versión nueva con estética urbana, vehículos, palmeras y luces de neón.
El proceso puede hacerse desde el celular y sin instalar un editor adicional. La calidad del resultado depende, en buena medida, de las imágenes elegidas y del nivel de detalle del texto que acompaña la solicitud.

Además, es útil revisar el tamaño del archivo antes de enviarlo. Una imagen borrosa, oscura o comprimida puede dificultar que la inteligencia artificial identifique detalles como el color del cabello, las prendas o los accesorios.

articles.title: AI discovers a hidden heart signal that could predict sudden death
articles.summary:
AI discovers a hidden heart signal that could predict sudden death
- Date:
  November 14, 2026
- Source:
  University of California - Berkeley
- Summary:
  Scientists have uncovered a hidden warning sign in routine heart scans that could predict sudden cardiac death before it strikes. The AI-powered discovery outperformed conventional screening methods, potentially revealing thousands of people at risk of a fatal heart malfunction that doctors might otherwise miss.
- Share:
More than 300,000 people in the United States die from sudden cardiac arrest each year. This deadly emergency occurs when the heart's electrical system suddenly fails, causing the heart to stop pumping blood. It can strike older adults with known heart conditions as well as seemingly healthy young athletes. Although implanted defibrillators can prevent some of these deaths, doctors have long struggled to determine which patients need them most.
Now, researchers at UC Berkeley have identified a previously overlooked warning signal in routine heart scans that could make it easier to recognize people at risk before a fatal event occurs.
The discovery was made using artificial intelligence trained on more than 440,000 electrocardiograms, or EKGs, collected in Sweden. articles.title: El Gobierno prorroga las ayudas al transporte público durante 2027: 1.213 millones para mantener los descuentos en tren y autobús
articles.summary:
El Gobierno ha prorrogado las subvenciones al transporte público hasta 2027, y lo ha hecho de ultimísimas. El Consejo de Ministros ha aprobado este martes un real decreto-ley, manteniendo vigentes los descuentos en metros, autobuses y trenes, así como el Abono Único, que iban a caducar el próximo 31 de diciembre. El Estado aportará 1.213 millones de euros.
Prórroga. Es una medida que afecta a millones de personas que dependen de abonos con descuento para su desplazamiento diario. Además, ha estado a punto de no entrar en vigor. Y es que tal y como cuentan desde El País, el Ministerio de Economía, que ha estado dirigiendo Transportes de forma interina desde la dimisión de Óscar Puente, prefería esperar hasta después de las elecciones para decidir. Pero claro, eso habría dejado los descuentos en el limbo durante meses.
Qué sigue igual. La mayoría de los descuentos actuales se mantienen:
- Ferrocarril: abono mensual de Cercanías y Rodalies a 20 euros (10 euros para jóvenes, gratuito para menores de 14 años). articles.title: Police disrupt 57 illegal streaming services with 7.3 million visits
articles.summary:
Law enforcement authorities from 11 countries have disrupted 57 illegal streaming services that operated hundreds of websites and drew over 7.3 million visits each year.
Such illegal IPTV services offer access to television channels, live sports, and movies without permission from the copyright owners for a small monthly fee.
According to the European Audiovisual Anti-Piracy Alliance (AAPA) trade association, legitimate service providers lose around €4.83 billion annually as roughly 60 million people in Europe use illegal platforms for streaming content.
"The operation resulted in the disruption of 57 illegal IPTV services and the identification of 321 websites illegally offering copyrighted content, with a combined annual traffic of more than 7.3 million visits. Investigators have so far traced over EUR 26 million in cryptocurrency transactions, with further analysis ongoing," Europol said in a Tuesday press release.
"The operation targeted a criminal market worth billions of euros annually, in which illegal streaming providers sell unauthorised access to premium television channels, live sports and films, often collecting subscription payments through cryptocurrency."

OpenClaw at one: its chief architect on a year of explosive growth, wooing the enterprise, and being Meta’s muse
It’s been a whirlwind 12 months for OpenClaw, the open source personal AI agent used for everything from managing calendars and email to booking flights and restaurants.
On Nov. 24, 2025 — exactly a year ago today — Austrian software developer Peter Steinberger made the first commit for Warelay, a small WhatsApp relay designed to let users trigger actions on their computer through WhatsApp. It briefly became Clawd, a play on Claude and its lobster mascot, before Anthropic’s legal team “politely” asked Steinberger to reconsider the name. After another short-lived stint as Moltbot, the project finally settled on OpenClaw at the end of January, 2026.
OpenClaw has become one of the most closely watched open source projects in AI. That excitement ultimately led OpenAI to hire Steinberger in February, with the project eventually moving into an independent foundation backed by companies including OpenAI itself, GitHub, and Nvidia.
Meanwhile, the Foundation has also stepped up its enterprise push, while the arrival of OpenClaw 2.0 focused heavily on making the project easier to install and use.
Ahead of the one-year anniversary, The New Stack caught up with Vincent Koc to chat all things OpenClaw, including how the project has matured, its growing enterprise ambitions, and how it has influenced projects from some of the biggest names in technology.

articles.title: Vehicle-to-Grid: Great Idea or Unrealistic Dream? (Part 2)
articles.summary:
Part 1 provided an overview of vehicle-to-grid (V2G) and its presumed benefits. This part looks at some real-world concerns and considerations.
V2G sounds good so far, but there are “issues”
Despite the presumed benefits, there are problems associated with V2G, starting with the charging hardware and technology. I suspect these will be worked out in a reasonable time, as vehicles increasingly come equipped with bidirectional chargers that can transfer power from the grid to the battery and send it back to the grid just as easily. Further, the higher-level management of the grid, power flows, supply/demand, pricing, monitoring, and other issues certainly are complicated, but let’s assume these, too, will eventually be worked out at some point.
It’s the implications of V2G that have me skeptical.
The good news is that it distributes energy storage, at least to a modest extent. That’s generally good for system resiliency, reliability, and integrity, at least in principle. V2G works on the premise that many cars and drivers will use only a fraction of their battery capacity most of the time; this approach optimizes battery utilization to get more out of the same components—that’s also a virtue.

articles.title: Designing A Microarchitecture From Formal Proof To Full-System
articles.summary:
Combining architectural proof, software-driven verification, simulation, emulation, and cloud-based compute infrastructure.
Data center and high-performance computing workloads are pushing CPU designers to deliver higher per-watt throughput and support complex multicore systems. Meeting these goals requires specialized compute cores. This reality is forcing engineers to rethink not only how cores are built, but also which instruction set architecture (ISA) can scale efficiently, support software validation, and still create product differentiation. To meet these challenges, a lean R&D team from a startup company in Austin, Texas, chose the RISC-V ISA as the foundation for its first CPU IP microarchitecture.
Designing the microarchitecture involved balancing software-visible architectural behavior, RTL implementation details, and internal performance and power tradeoffs, which together introduced verification requirements that extended well beyond isolated hardware blocks. When these interactions are not addressed early in development, system-level issues can emerge later, making them more difficult to resolve. These decisions also expanded the scope of verification. The core had to be validated with actual software under full-system scale, including interactions that extend beyond individual hardware blocks.

articles.title: Data centers are getting their own natural gas power plants
articles.summary:
Data centers are getting their own natural gas power plants
The numbers behind the off-grid gas power boom.
One of the biggest roadblocks to starting up a data center is getting approval to connect to the electric grid—a wait that could last as long as a decade. Some developers aren’t willing to wait and are instead opting to build their own off-grid, or behind-the-meter, gas power plants to fuel the AI boom.
xAI’s Memphis campus has famously used dozens of natural gas turbines, some of them without permits, as far back as 2024. At the time, that facility was a rarity, and it faced scrutiny from regulators. It remains the subject of ongoing legal battles. But the strategy of going off-grid for power has since become a lot more common.
As of October 2026, data center developers have announced plans for more than 100 behind-the-meter gas power plants at facilities in the US, according to data from Cleanview, a market intelligence company. The facilities have a combined planned capacity of over 115 gigawatts, more than double the peak power demand of California. The vast majority of these announcements have come since the beginning of 2025.
It’s possible that not all these facilities will be built; only a small fraction are under construction or operating today. But there’s a growing trend of large data centers looking to build their own power supply, and this could shape the grid—and its climate impacts—for decades to come.

Ariane 6 devait emporter 36 nouveaux satellites dès le lundi 23 novembre, mais un problème technique sur les installations au sol a interrompu le compte à rebours.
La fusée européenne est finalement partie de Kourou ce mardi 24 novembre à 8h14, heure locale (12h14 à Paris), et l’Agence spatiale européenne (ESA) a diffusé les images du décollage sur X.
Les images du décollages de la fusée Ariane 6, pour son 10e tir
Il s’en est fallu de peu : la chronologie a encore été arrêtée quelques minutes avant le tir par une alerte rouge sur l’ensemble de lancement. Ariane 6 a ensuite pu décoller, à la toute fin de sa fenêtre de tir prévue.

articles.title: We Get the Infrastructure We Pay For
articles.summary:
We Get the Infrastructure We Pay For
This essay originally appeared as part of a round table in The Free Press entitled “Is America’s Infrastructure Under Attack?”
Microsoft, the FAA, banks, United Airlines, the NSA—it’s been a really bad week in cyberspace. But, amazing as it might seem, these are not related. As far as we know, they’re not the result of cyberattacks. They’re not even related to AI. (Well, that’s mostly true. The NSA will probably never tell us what went wrong.) It’s really just a series of unfortunate coincidences.
Our computerized infrastructure is vulnerable and fragile. Much of it is old, and has been incrementally patched and upgraded. A surprising amount of it is maintained by hobbyists, without any recompense. And more and more of it is centralized: the same systems affecting many different aspects of our lives and society. In many cases, it just barely works. And when it fails, it tends to fail badly.
There are a lot of technological reasons why this is true, but they are all downstream of the economic ones. The technologies we rely on are built and maintained within our economic system—and that’s where the core problem lies.
Security, safety, resilience, redundancy, recoverability—these are all essential parts of reliable technology, but they are all costs.
More importantly, they are inefficient: costs that feel wasteful until something bad happens. Modern shareholder capitalism, and private equity in particular, squeeze all inefficiencies out of a …

articles.summary:
Amazon said AI agents recently found and exploited a zero-day vulnerability with no human oversight beyond a simple instruction to get root access on an East Asian university server.
The agents were running on Cairn, an open source AI penetration-testing framework. The hackers, who provided prompts in simplified Chinese and configured the model to the Chinese Standard Time zone, gave the agents a list of IP addresses and the goal: “obtain shell access.” In short order, the agents discovered a zero-day in an open source medical imaging AI application running on one of the target servers. The agents then exploited the vulnerability and gained full control of the system.
“These findings show that agentic offensive operations are already happening, and defenders should prepare for the speed and persistence these tools enable,” Amazon said.
Made for defenders, but attackers like it too
Cairn is an open source AI problem-solving engine whose first validated domain is autonomous penetration testing. Users give it a task or goal and, optionally, hints for achieving it. A server maintains a shared graph containing facts and hints. A dispatcher reads the graph, schedules tasks, manages containers, and writes the protocol. The dispatcher can then assign each project to a dedicated worker container, each of which runs multiple agents concurrently. First look: Ladybird, an independent web browser running on a rendering engine its developers wrote from scratch, is now available for alpha testing on macOS and Linux. Developer Andreas Kling announced the release Monday after more than four years of work. It is the first browser in years not to run on Gecko, Blink, or WebKit, the three engines behind today's most popular browsers.
Most browser makers start from an existing engine and build features on top of it. Ladybird's team wrote its own, so every part of the browser, from how pages are laid out to how they are drawn on screen, comes from code the project controls instead of code it inherited.
Ladybird started as part of a C++ project, but its developers later began porting the code to Rust using AI. That means testers are getting a codebase that is partway through a move from one language to another, with AI tools helping with the rewrite.
For engineers, this makes Ladybird a live test of whether AI-assisted porting can work at the scale of a full browser engine.
Kling is candid about the browser's current limitations. In his announcement, he said the browser built around the Ladybird engine "is modest but functional." He also warned that "some websites won't work" during the alpha. A new engine has a lot of ground to cover before it can handle the full range of sites people use every day, and the alpha is meant to show where it still falls short.

articles.title: Plus forte que la RTX 5090 ? Ce qu'on sait de la carte graphique Moore Threads Lushan équipée de 64 Go de VRAM

La VRAM, c’est cette mémoire ultra-rapide soudée directement sur la carte graphique, où un modèle d’IA doit tenir en entier pour rester fluide (s’il déborde sur la RAM classique du PC, les performances s’effondrent).
Le record actuel appartient à la RTX 5090 et ses 32 Go, vendue environ 7 000 euros en France.
Publié le 18 novembre sur les réseaux sociaux chinois, le message provient d’un chef de produit de la MTT S80, la carte actuelle de la marque. Les détails officiels tomberont lors de la MDC 2026, sa conférence développeurs organisée les 29 et 30 décembre à Pékin.
Lushan avait déjà été évoquée en décembre 2025 aux côtés de Huagang, la nouvelle architecture maison destinée à remplacer les MTT S80 et S90. Moore Threads promettait alors de quadrupler la mémoire de la MTT S80 (qui compte 16 Go), d’où la rumeur tenace des 64 Go qui circule aujourd’hui sans aucune confirmation officielle.
Ce que l’on attend
Les multiplicateurs avancés par la marque donnent le vertige : 15 fois plus de performances en jeu, 50 fois en ray tracing et 64 fois en IA. Getting a GPU is only the beginning. Ask AWS EKS.
Eight minutes is a long time to wait for another copy of an AI model to start serving traffic. It feels longer when the requests are already coming in. And while Kubernetes can schedule another replica, there’s still hardware to provision, a container image to pull, model weights to load, and GPU code to compile.
The autoscaler got the message, but the model is still getting dressed.

Their conversation starts with the scramble to find GPUs and gets into the engineering decisions that determine how much work those GPUs actually do.
“Demand for GPU capacity or any accelerated capacity is outpacing supply everywhere,” Gundapunnedi told TNS.
Give Kubernetes more to do
In our interview, Gundapunnedi describes two ways to line up accelerated capacity through EKS Auto Mode and Karpenter, the Kubernetes node provisioner. On-Demand Capacity Reservations secure capacity in a specific Availability Zone, subject to availability. Capacity Blocks let teams book capacity for a fixed future window. That gives teams planning a training or fine-tuning run a way to schedule the job around a reservation.
“What this lets you do is faster communication for your job,” Gundapunnedi told TNS.

articles.title: De una isla retiraron 131 gatos, y luego sucedió algo que incluso sorprendió a los científicos
articles.summary:
En 2008, las palomas de cabeza roja de Ogasawara (un archipiélago japonés) era crítica, ya que quedaban menos de 80 ejemplares por culpa de los gatos asilvestrados que llegaron a esas islas por la acción humana. Dos años después, empezó una campaña para capturarlos que terminó con 131 gatos retirados de Chichijima, una de las islas del archipiélago, y lo curioso llegó después cuando los científicos comprobaron que las aves se recuperaban a una velocidad por encima de lo esperado.
Tres años después, los registros de palomas adultas pasaron de 111 a 966, e incluso los ejemplares más jóvenes aumentaron de 9 a 189. Se trata de un crecimiento enorme para una subespecie (Columba janthina nitens) que solo vive a unos 1.000 kilómetros del territorio principal de Japón, pero todavía queda una pregunta por resolver que va más allá de de la retirada de gatos: ¿cómo consiguieron recuperarse tan rápido?
Una recuperación que también tenía una explicación genética
Un equipo de la Universidad de Kioto, encabezado por Daichi Tsujimoto, decidió investigar qué estaba pasando. En un estudio publicado en Communications Biology en julio de 2025, analizaron el ADN de estas palomas y lo compararon con el de otras poblaciones emparentadas. Descubrieron que más del 80 % de su genoma presentaba homocigosidad (una señal de reproducción entre individuos emparentados), pero tenían menos mutaciones especialmente perjudiciales de las que cabría esperar.

Et s’il était possible de décrire à Gemini la voix que vous souhaitez utiliser ? C’est la nouvelle fonction sur laquelle semble travailler Google.

articles.title: Why Photonic Design Is Becoming a System-Level Challenge
articles.summary:
A component can meet its individual design targets and still behave differently as part of a complete optical link.
Photonic engineers make design decisions at many levels.
A laser has its own performance requirements. So does an optical fiber. The interface between them introduces another set of variables. Ultimately, those individual components have to perform together as part of a complete optical link.
If the individual pieces meet their design targets, will the complete system perform as expected?
Not necessarily.
A Keysight EDA-Photonics Design (VPIphotonics) study of short-reach datacenter links provides a useful example. Two multimode VCSEL channels were designed with comparable signal characteristics and evaluated with a wideband multimode fiber. Yet when evaluated as complete transmission links, the two channels produced different results.
Understanding the difference in performance requires looking beyond any single component.
The VPIphotonics study modeled 26.5625 GBaud PAM4 transmission over 150 meters of wideband multimode fiber, using VCSEL channels operating at 850 nm and 910 nm. Each VCSEL was modeled with four transverse modes, and the link considered coupling conditions and receiver models.
25 Gbaud PAM4 with a multimode VCSEL and OM4 fiber.
At first glance, the two channels seemed comparable.
The calculated 3 dB bandwidth was 27.0 GHz at 850 nm and 27.8 GHz at 910 nm.
But that wasn’t the end of the story.

Cómo usarlo, paso a paso
Primero, entrar al Modo IA desde el navegador. Segundo, seleccionar la opción “Temporary thread” (hilo temporal), arriba a la derecha. El sitio de ayuda de Google resalta que también se pueden subir imágenes y archivos desde el menú, o consultar por voz con el micrófono.

La historia del hacker que filtró GTA 6 siendo un adolescente ha dado un giro bastante curioso. "Que no vuelva a suceder", le manifestó el magistrado a Arion Kurtaj, según publica BBC. Entre las firmas impactadas estuvo Rockstar Games, que padeció la divulgación de una gran cantidad de vídeos de GTA 6 cuando su desarrollo todavía estaba lejos de finalizado.
Uno de los puntos más curiosos de aquel incidente fue que Kurtaj hackeó Rockstar desde la habitación de un hotel, usando un Fire TV Stick. El por entonces adolescente intentó extorsionar al estudio para evitar la filtración de los materiales de GTA 6, pero estos acabaron divulgándose en Twitter y servidores de Discord.
Cuando la policía finalmente dio con el paradero de Arion Kurtaj, la justicia decidió mantenerlo internado por tiempo indefinido en una institución psiquiátrica debido a la severidad de su autismo. Asimismo, se determinó que esta era la mejor opción de supervivencia del hacker de GTA 6, debido a que piratas informáticos rivales lo doxxearon y amenazaron su integridad física en múltiples oportunidades.

Tidal is also banning distribution services from delivering 100% AI-generated tracks, and will reject submissions if songs’ metadata says they are made fully using AI.
The company said it will still accept songs that were made with AI assistance, but not fully generated.
The move comes as AI-generated music inundates streaming services across the board. Tidal is one of the first major platforms after Bandcamp to ban AI music outright. Deezer, which also provides detection tools to other streaming services, said that it will introduce a toggle to let users filter out AI music. Larger platforms like Spotify and YouTube Music have adopted a milder approach to this issue, choosing to label AI-generated music instead of offering filters or taking stronger measures.

articles.title: As MCP turns two, Claude gets Skills over MCP and better support for long-running tasks

As MCP turns two, Claude gets Skills over MCP and better support for long-running tasks
Anthropic on Tuesday marked the second anniversary of the Model Context Protocol (MCP) by bringing support for skills, long-running tasks, and file uploads over MCP to Claude.
Skills over MCP, which lets MCP servers publish skills alongside their tools, is now available in public beta, while Tasks, which first landed in Claude Code as a beta in October, and Elicitation are now generally available. File uploads will roll out soon.
All three are meant to help agents work more autonomously and for longer stretches of time, which, according to the protocol’s maintainers, is also where the project focused much of its second year. In its announcement, Anthropic says these features let Claude treat an MCP server more like another agent that it can learn from and delegate work to.
Den Delimarsky, a lead maintainer of MCP at Anthropic, tells The New Stack, “You have long-running tasks, you have events, you have file uploads and downloads, you have skills over MCP, and all of them working together now enable a completely different spectrum of scenarios.”
From early adoption to agents
When Anthropic first launched MCP in November 2024, it wasn’t clear whether the protocol would pan out, says David Soria Parra, who co-created MCP at Anthropic and remains one of its lead maintainers. That first year was mostly about adoption, he says.

articles.title: Browser auf dem iPhone: Warum Mozilla und 55.000 andere Unternehmen die EU auffordern, gegen Apple vorzugehen

Browser auf dem iPhone: Warum Mozilla und 55.000 andere Unternehmen die EU auffordern, gegen Apple vorzugehen
Ein Bündnis aus Mozilla, dem E-Commerce-Anbieter Shopify und über 50.000 Firmen aus der EU fordert von der Europäischen Kommission ein Verfahren samt Strafen gegen Apple. In einem offenen Brief „für mehr Wettbewerb im Web“ und ein „stärkeres Europa“ sprechen die Unterzeichner Kommissionspräsidentin Ursula von der Leyen direkt an.
Worum es im Streit geht
Im Zentrum steht die sogenannte Browser-Engine – also der technische Unterbau, der Webseiten darstellt. Auf iPhone und iPad schreibt Apple außerhalb der EU und Japans vor, dass alle Browser Apples eigene Engine WebKit nutzen. Selbst Googles Chrome läuft dort deshalb mit Apple-Technik.
In der Europäischen Union ist das anders: Durch den Digital Markets Act (DMA), die EU-Regeln für besonders marktmächtige Plattformen, dürfen Entwickler seit knapp drei Jahren eigene Engines auf iOS und iPadOS anbieten. Apple ist dabei als sogenannter Gatekeeper reguliert. In Japan gilt eine ähnliche Regelung seit Dezember 2025.
Warum bislang niemand mitmacht
Genutzt hat die neuen Möglichkeiten bisher aber kein großer Anbieter. Der Grund: Es ist kompliziert. Mozilla kritisiert, Apples Bedingungen seien „nicht praktikabel“, weil Entwickler eigene App-Pakete allein für die EU bauen und pflegen müssten. articles.title: GTA VI PC recompilation project shut down by Take-Two

Game modding communities are racing to get Grand Theft Auto VI running on PC, but one big effort has been taken down by Take-Two today. Leonida, a fan project by 15-year-old “NotRexed,” has vanished after a DMCA takedown notice from GTA VI publisher Take-Two.
GTA VI PC recompilation project shut down by Take-Two
Modders are racing to get Grand Theft Auto VI running on PC.
Leonida was designed to translate a leaked GTA VI Xbox build to run natively on Windows. Cyberleek, the leaker who posted multiple GTA VI gameplay videos over the summer, published a full Xbox build of the game earlier this week. The leak has kicked recompilation efforts up a notch, as modders race to reverse-engineer the game’s code and rebuild it into native PC code.

- Date:

- Source:

  AI may not think like the human brain after all, according to a striking new discovery that challenges how scientists understand artificial intelligence. Researchers found that even AI models that closely predict brain activity may rely on internal processes the brain doesn't use, raising important questions about their reliability in neuroscience research.
- Share:
Artificial intelligence may be much less like the human brain than scientists have long assumed. A new study from York University has uncovered a surprising weakness in AI models that are widely used to understand how the brain processes visual information.
For years, researchers have relied on artificial neural networks (ANNs), computer systems designed to perform tasks such as recognizing objects in images, to investigate how vision works. Over the past decade, these models have become some of the leading tools for explaining the brain's visual system. Their ability to reproduce patterns of brain activity has made them especially valuable in neuroscience.
But the new findings raise an important question: Just because AI can successfully imitate certain responses in the brain, does that mean it actually processes visual information in the same way?

The breach did not involve any classified information and the issue has been resolved, said the person, who was not authorized to speak by name and spoke on condition of anonymity.
The breach affected a system that handles open source intelligence, which involves the collection and analysis of publicly available data from sources including the internet, commercial satellites and private data brokers. articles.title: Australia threatens US tech giants with fines of up to 5% of global revenue over online safety

Winners & losers: Australia is threatening to slam US tech giants with penalties that could reach into the billions of dollars. The country says that unless these companies take reasonable steps to protect users from harmful content and addictive features on their platforms, they could be fined up to 5% of their global revenue.
Australia's Labor government struck a deal with the Greens on Tuesday that gives its Digital Duty of Care bill the support it needs to pass the Senate. The original proposal capped fines at A$109.2 million, or about US$72 million. But even that amount looks modest next to what a company the size of Meta could face under the revised bill.
In Meta's case, that would be around $10 billion based on its 2025 revenue, while the same calculation for Google parent Alphabet comes to about $20 billion.
The changes would also give Australians who suffer harm the right to sue a platform directly, opening the door to class actions. For someone with a smaller claim, going to court might be more trouble than it's worth. The deal would let the government set up an independent ombudsman to handle those complaints.
For users, anyone aged 16 or older could turn off algorithmic recommendations and see posts only from accounts they follow. The bill would also require platforms to tackle risks to children, including bullying and material promoting eating disorders. Otros cinco kilómetros entre Salas y el viaducto de El Regueirón están abiertos desde noviembre de 2022.
