La serie de God of War ha confirmado a un nuevo fichaje de primer nivel. Se trata de Deborah Ann Woll, quien interpretará a Faye en la adaptación que Amazon MGM Studios prepara para la plataforma Prime Video. De esta manera, la actriz regresará al papel que ya interpretó en los videojuegos.
Deborah Ann Woll dio vida a Faye por primera vez en God of War Ragnarok (2022), prestando su voz como guía de Kratos y Atreus en su aventura. Muy pronto, tendrá la oportunidad de liderar su primera aventura en solitario de la mano de God of War Laufey, que llegará en 2027. Dicho juego no solo utilizará la voz de la intérprete, sino también su apariencia.
Todavía no se sabe cuánto peso en pantalla tendrá Deborah Ann Woll en la adaptación televisiva de God of War, pero Faye es un personaje crucial en la historia. Tengamos en cuenta que la serie se basa en el juego de 2018, que se inicia con el fallecimiento de la esposa de Kratos y madre de Atreus. Esto llevará a que los protagonistas pongan en marcha un largo peregrinar para arrojar sus cenizas en el pico más alto de los nueve reinos.
"God of War sigue a Kratos y a su hijo Atreus mientras emprenden un viaje para esparcir las cenizas de Faye, esposa de uno y madre del otro. A lo largo de sus aventuras, Kratos intenta enseñar a su hijo a ser un mejor dios, mientras que Atreus trata de enseñarle a su padre cómo ser un mejor ser humano", indica la sinopsis oficial de la serie de Prime Video.

articles.title: Meta brings its Muse AI assistant directly into Instagram DMs
articles.summary:
Instagram users can now chat with Meta’s AI agent Muse in a DM thread, the company announced on Tuesday. The social media network says users can chat with Muse to get more context about a post, place, or product they come across, or catch up on conversations they may have missed in their other DMs.
The new integration gets rid of the need for users to toggle between Instagram and the Muse app when they want to interact with the AI agent. It also reflects the growing competition among tech companies to make AI assistants a part of users’ everyday digital lives. By embedding Muse directly into Instagram, Meta is making it easier for users to access the AI agent, while also giving Muse access to a platform where users already discover products, places, and content.
Users can share Instagram posts with Muse and ask it to take action, such as adding a coffee shop to their Mexico City itinerary or finding a Black Friday deal on a pair of shoes.
Meta notes that conversations with Muse on Instagram will appear as a side chat in the main Muse app.
Muse in Instagram DMs will begin rolling out on Tuesday for iOS and Android users in the U.S., Canada, Mexico, Japan, and Singapore.
Meta also announced that users can now do more with the posts and reels they’ve bookmarked on Instagram. For example, they can ask Muse to organize their saved content into custom folders, known as Collections. articles.title: Hope Is Not A Strategy: What First-Silicon Success Really Takes
articles.summary:
Most re-spins are caused by logic and functional flaws, not hard-to-predict physical effects.
Only about one chip in twenty now works the first time it comes back from the fab. For an industry that invests years and millions in every tape-out, that is a disconcerting thought.
It was also the starting point for a recent episode of ‘Wearing Flip Flops’, where host Ronen sat down with Axiomise CEO Ashish Darbari. The conversation traveled from AI silicon and power bugs to the place of formal engineers in a verification team. But one idea ran through all of it: Hope is not a strategy. Determinism is.
Here is what that idea means in practice and why we believe it matters more today than ever.
The latest Wilson Research Group functional verification study puts first-silicon success at around 5%, down from 14% in 2024. At Axiomise, that number doesn’t surprise us.
Look at who is building chips. Two years ago, the survey was shaped by a wave of new RISC-V teams, where design was moving faster than verification could follow. Today it is the turn of custom AI silicon, built not only for hyperscalers but for phones and cars too. For verification, this is an unknown territory.
Formal is in more projects than ever, perhaps 30 to 40% of them. But “using formal” can mean very different things. It might be a lint or connectivity app, assertions that only ever run in simulation, or formal trusted to sign off functional verification. Only the last really improves the chances of success at tape…

articles.title: Huawei found guilty of stealing trade secrets
articles.summary:
A jury has found Huawei guilty of stealing US trade secrets, as reported earlier by NBC News and Bloomberg. The verdict, handed down in a federal court in New York, concludes a years-long legal battle that accused the Chinese telecom giant of stealing source code and proprietary technology from several companies, including T-Mobile, Cisco, and Motorola.
Huawei found guilty of stealing trade secrets
The Chinese telecom giant was also found guilty of bank fraud.
The Department of Justice’s 2018 criminal indictment against Huawei came to light following the arrest of the company’s CFO, Wanzhou Meng, whom the agency accused of fraud. Though the indictment against Meng was eventually dismissed, she admitted to misleading banks over Huawei’s operations in Iran as part of a deferred prosecution agreement. The US government blacklisted Huawei in 2019 over national security concerns.
In total, the jury found Huawei guilty of 10 of 12 criminal counts, including money laundering, violating US sanctions, bank fraud, wire fraud, and conspiracy to defraud the US. The company was acquitted of engaging in a criminal racketeering conspiracy and obstruction of justice. Huawei’s sentencing is set for September 14th, 2027, where it may face “financial penalties including criminal fines, forfeiture, and restitution,” according to the DOJ.

articles.title: Bcomp secures €20 million from EIB to scale flax fibre-based alternatives to carbon fibre, glass fibre and plastics
articles.summary:
Bcomp, a Fribourg-based CleanTech startup specialising in high-performance bio-based materials, has secured €20 million from the European Investment Bank (EIB) to build a high-volume manufacturing plant in the Romanian city of Timișoara and continue research and development in Fribourg.
This EIB backing takes the form of €20 million in venture debt, supporting the company’s €47.6 million investment programme to expand manufacturing capacity in Romania and further develop its R&D activities in Switzerland. In April 2024, the company closed a €37.6 million Series C investment funding round led by EGS Beteiligungen AG (EGSB), and in April 2022, it closed its oversubscribed Series B financing round of €31.69 million (CHF 32.4 million/USD 35 million).
“Europe needs to turn technological innovation into industrial production if we are to strengthen our competitiveness and accelerate the green transition. By supporting Bcomp in Romania and Switzerland, we are helping European innovation reach industrial scale and unlock new opportunities for sustainable growth,” said EIB Vice-President Ioannis Tsakiris.
Founded in 2011 by Christian Fischer and Julien Rion, Bcomp develops composite materials based primarily on flax fibres instead of conventional carbon fibre, glass fibre and plastics. The company says its materials, which have a significantly lower environmental footprint, are designed for use in a range of industries, including automotive, motorsport, and recreational equipment.

articles.title: Canada’s Scott Pilgrim is coming to Fortnite
articles.summary:
Fortnite just got a little more Canadian.
Developer Epic Games has announced that skins based on Scott Pilgrim and Ramona Flowers are coming to its popular battle royale game sometime this week.
In a short trailer, we can see the Toronto couple in creator Bryan Lee O’Malley’s signature comic book style. Scott sports his jacket, star t-shirt, guitar and flaming sword, while Ramona has her punk outfit and hammer. Naturally, the trailer also riffs on Scott Pilgrim‘s fighting game-style battles with the evil exes and Envy Adams music.
Epic Games didn’t confirm the V-Bucks cost for Scott and Ramona or what else, if anything, this collab might include. In the meantime, though, O’Malley shared fun new artwork of the pair dropping from the Fortnite Battle Bus.
It’s been a good year for everyone’s favourite sword-wielding Torontonian. In March, Montreal-based Tribute Games released Scott Pilgrim EX, a brand-new beat ’em up featuring an original story by O’Malley.

articles.title: Homo erectus lived in the rainforest alongside Denisovans
articles.summary:
This artist's illustration shows one take on what Homo erectus might have looked like in its rainforest home near Baxian Cave, Guangxi, China.
Credit:
Garciart/Joannes-Boyau
This artist's illustration shows one take on what Homo erectus might have looked like in its rainforest home near Baxian Cave, Guangxi, China.
Credit:
Garciart/Joannes-Boyau
Homo erectus was walking around mainland Asia at least 60,000 years more recently than archaeologists thought. A handful of teeth from two caves in southern China’s Guangxi Province just filled in a significant gap in the fossil record of a region that’s vital to the story of how our genus, Homo, took over the world.
The chemical makeup of the teeth’s enamel suggests that, over the course of their lives, these Homo erectus moved across surprisingly large distances and made their living in dense tropical rainforests—an environment we’d previously assumed that only our species had ever gained a real foothold in. And one of the teeth offers a strong clue that Homo erectus probably shared this vast landscape with the Denisovans.
A handful of teeth with a lot to say
Baxian and Naxian are a pair of limestone caves that lie 15 kilometers apart along a karst valley corridor in southern China. University of Copenhagen paleoanthropologist Frido Welker and his colleagues unearthed a total of nine hominin teeth from among the more than 18,000 bones and fragments from non-hominin animals found there. articles.title: Xbox Helix started as a PC in disguise, with free multiplayer and Steam, until plans changed
articles.summary:
What we know so far: Microsoft has confirmed that the next Xbox, codenamed Helix, will support PC games, but the extent of that support remains unclear. Current messaging indicates a console-first experience, but rumors suggest the project initially leaned in a much more PC-centric direction. It remains uncertain how much Microsoft's current roadmap resembles that original plan.
Sources tell Windows Central that, before Asha Sharma became Xbox CEO earlier this year, Microsoft planned for its next console to essentially be a PC with an Xbox-style UI and support for Xbox console games. This would have required the company to drop its online multiplayer paywall.
As prior rumors suggested, the Asus ROG Xbox Ally was a rough draft of the experience the Xbox division intended for its next console while under Phil Spencer. The next Xbox would have run on Windows and booted into Microsoft's new Xbox Mode by default, but users could exit to the traditional desktop and install any Windows app, including Steam.
Microsoft's official messaging remains vague but implies the opposite approach while retaining some PC compatibility. The company recently described its next console, now codenamed Helix, as a console that plays PC games, not a PC that plays console games.
The device will feature a new interface that provides immediate access to games but also supports greater customization for advanced users and eliminates traditional barriers. However, it remains unclear what this means and how…

articles.title: AI uncovers hidden bladder cancer warning signs years before diagnosis
articles.summary:
AI uncovers hidden bladder cancer warning signs years before diagnosis
- Date:
  November 21, 2026
- Source:
  University of Plymouth
- Summary:
  Scientists have developed an AI tool that can uncover hidden warning signs of bladder cancer up to five years before diagnosis, identifying 85% of cases in a major study involving nearly 70,000 patients. By revealing subtle patterns that conventional screening misses, the technology could help doctors detect cancer earlier and spare patients unnecessary invasive procedures.
- Share:
Bladder cancer kills approximately 220,000 people worldwide each year, yet recognizing the disease early can be difficult. Its symptoms can resemble those of far less serious conditions, including kidney stones, allowing warning signs to go unnoticed.
Researchers at the University of Plymouth have now developed an artificial intelligence system that could help doctors identify people at risk of bladder cancer years before they receive a diagnosis. In some patients, the technology detected subtle warning signals dating back as far as five years.
The new approach uses AI to examine electronic health records, searching for combinations of symptoms, medical conditions, risk factors, and healthcare activity that might otherwise be overlooked. By recognizing these patterns, researchers hope to make bladder cancer screening more accurate and help doctors find the disease when treatment is most likely to succeed.

Le PlayStation Portal est affiché à 249,99 € chez Cdiscount, et passe à 239,99 € avec le code 10DES99 à saisir dans le panier pendant le Black Friday. C’est dix euros de moins que son prix public, fixé depuis la hausse décidée par Sony en avril 2026.
GTA 6 sans PS5 ? Oui mais à deux conditions
Jusqu’ici, le Portal ne lançait GTA 6 qu’en lecture à distance : il affichait, via le Wi-Fi, l’image d’une PS5 allumée ou en veille dans le salon. Depuis ce lundi 23 novembre, le jeu de Rockstar est aussi disponible en streaming cloud. Il tourne alors sur les serveurs de Sony, et la console devient facultative. L’exclusivité dont profitait Xbox Cloud Gaming avec la Xbox One n’aura duré que quatre jours.
Il faut toutefois remplir deux conditions. La première, c’est de posséder le jeu, vendu 79,99 € en édition Standard, puisqu’il ne fait pas partie du catalogue du PlayStation Plus. La version boîte ne contient qu’un code de téléchargement : une fois activée, elle rejoint votre bibliothèque numérique comme un achat sur le PlayStation Store, et devrait donc ouvrir les mêmes droits. La seconde, c’est d’être abonné au PlayStation Plus Premium, la formule la plus chère du service : 18,99 € par mois, 54,99 € pour trois mois ou 151,99 € pour un an. Les sauvegardes sont stockées en ligne, ce qui permet de reprendre sur le Portal une partie commencée sur une PS5.

articles.summary:
Comme tous les constructeurs, Samsung doit composer avec la montée des prix des composants, comme la mémoire RAM, mais aussi des coûts de fabrication. Selon des informations qui viennent directement de la chaîne d’approvisionnement, les futures Galaxy A38 et Galaxy A58 pourraient souffrir de ces contraintes. Cela se traduirait notamment par une partie photo qui ferait du surplace par rapport à la génération précédente, voire qui ferait un pas en arrière.
Un capteur photo moins bon pour le Galaxy A38 ?
Sur le papier, le futur Galaxy A38 afficherait toujours un bloc caméra principal de 50 mégapixels. Pourtant, certains documents indiquent que Samsung testerait un capteur Sony IMX882 pour ce modèle. Ce serait donc une régression par rapport au Galaxy A37, qui embarque un Sony IMX906 sur de nombreux marchés. Le capteur IMX882 propose une surface de 1/1,95 pouce, nettement plus petite que les 1/1,56 pouce du IMX906. Dans les faits, Samsung réutiliserait un composant déjà présent sur le Galaxy A36, sorti deux générations plus tôt.
Un capteur plus petit, c’est moins de lumière, ce qui vient dégrader les photos en basse luminosité ainsi que le flou d’arrière-plan naturel (bokeh). articles.title: Vancouver considering stricter rules, oversight for AI data centres
articles.summary:
Vancouver City Council has unanimously directed City of Vancouver staff to examine stronger oversight of new data centres, including third-party assessments of their effects on the surrounding area, public reporting on their operations, and ways to secure benefits for local residents.
OneCity city councillor Lucy Maloney’s member motion, approved last week after amendments, asks City staff to develop recommendations on how the municipal government should assess and regulate data centres as artificial intelligence (AI) facilities grow.
“This is about ensuring we move forward responsibly and thoughtfully. As we’ve seen in the United States, hyperscale data centres can bring significant challenges. Compared to many other industrial businesses, data centres are often far more resource intensive, placing greater strain on public infrastructure. They can consume vast quantities of water and energy while producing pollution, waste heat, and noise. They also tend to create fewer jobs than other industrial uses of the land,” said Maloney during the City Council meeting.
“Furthermore, the economic benefits to host communities often fall short of the returns realised by investors by a long shot. This is a global issue, not just limited to the U.S. Cities worldwide are sharing best practices to develop effective frameworks and ensure data centres represent the best use of valuable land,” continued Maloney.

articles.title: Electric truck startup Harbinger gets financing boost from Palmer Luckey's bank
articles.summary:
Harbinger has tapped Palmer Luckey’s Erebor Bank as a new source of capital as the electric truck startup looks to diversify how it funds its growth and an expanding portfolio of products spanning autonomous vehicles, energy storage, and defense.
Los Angeles-based Harbinger said Tuesday it secured more than $100 million in financing, including a convertible note from Pinegrove Venture Partners and senior debt from Erebor Bank, which launched in February 2026 and recently surpassed $1 billion in loans, according to the Financial Times.
The new financing comes less than three weeks after Harbinger raised $240 million in a Series D funding round co-led by Tiger Global, Capricorn’s Technology Impact Fund, and Ridgeline. FedEx, which ordered 2,000 trucks from Harbinger, also participated.
Harbinger co-founder and chief executive John Harris explained in a statement that building an industrial technology company at scale requires a “different financing approach,” adding that the capital needed to ramp up production and deliver vehicles to customers shouldn’t have to come entirely from equity. Harris noted that major vehicle and aerospace manufacturers have long relied on debt financing to support their production operations.
Erebor is now Harbinger’s primary banking partner. In a statement, Luckey said traditional lenders have struggled to support the unique capital needs of businesses developing real technology and creating U.S. jobs.

articles.title: NASA may get $2 billion boost as White House seeks to accelerate Artemis
articles.summary:
As part of ongoing wrangling over the US budget for the current fiscal year, the White House on Monday night sent a list of budget exceptions to Congress that it seeks in the near term for the federal government (PDF).
The list of so-called “funding anomalies” is dominated largely by appropriations for the Department of Defense, including the Golden Dome missile defense program championed by the Trump administration. However, among the highest non-defense exceptions is $2 billion for NASA’s Artemis program for a “higher rate of operations.”
The funding represents a significant 25 percent boost for NASA’s Artemis program, which received approximately $7.8 billion in fiscal year 2026. Technically, the White House is seeking to increase the annualized funding rate for Artemis to $9.8 billion, rather than immediately providing NASA with an additional $2 billion. It comes at a time when it is increasingly clear that China’s lunar ambitions are as expansive as NASA’s, and there is a good chance the country reaches the Moon with astronauts before NASA can get back there.
Another continuing resolution?
Fiscal year 2027 began on October 1 of this year, but the US Congress and White House have not agreed upon a budget. The government, including NASA, has been operating on a “continuing resolution” since that time. articles.title: Banks and card networks raid Safaricom, Airtel for talent
articles.summary:
African banks and Visa have poached at least six senior executives from telecoms and mobile money companies this year, bringing in leaders from Safaricom, M‑PESA Africa, Airtel Money, and MTN to run businesses spanning retail banking, payments, and technology.
Four of the six hires came from Safaricom or M‑PESA Africa. The appointments show how competition over who handles everyday payments is changing where financial companies hire.
Mobile money operators have built merchant networks and used them to extend wallets into savings, lending, and investments. Banks are now trying to bring more of those activities into their own apps, while Visa is looking for more ways to reach customers and merchants who already use mobile wallets.
Kenya’s banks and telcos have been recruiting from one another for at least a decade. Safaricom hired Ronald Webb from Equity Bank to run its financial services business in 2016. It recruited Michael Mutiga from Citi in 2022 and Esther Masese Waititu from KCB in 2023. Waititu’s move set off another hire. The conclusion is either that China has solved robotics and we (Europe) are finished, or that they have adopted everything and we are just behind.
So we went to look. In August, six of us from Extantia visited around fifteen companies across Shanghai, Hangzhou and Beijing, then walked the floor of the World Robot Conference with its 300 exhibitors.
So, what is real?
The gap between the hype and reality
Much of what you see on Instagram is AI-generated while a lot of the rest is sped up. What looks autonomous is often teleoperated, or remote controlled
The reality is this: Chinese companies sold more humanoid robots than anyone last year. Roughly 75% went to research institutes, universities and schools. Another 20% went to entertainment: the robot that greets you at the supermarket, 50 robots dancing at a Chinese New Year show. Only 5% went to real industrial applications, 5% of maybe 13,000 units.

Le split tunneling, ou « tunnel fractionné », consiste à trier le trafic qui passe ou non par le VPN activé sur le système. D’ordinaire, cela permet de couper le VPN sur certaines applications. Firefox 161 applique ce principe site par site. Selon Mozilla, le VPN ne tourne qu’aux endroits où l’on veut plus de confidentialité ou une autre localisation. Il sera par exemple possible de l’activer en consultant sa messagerie ou pour éviter le ciblage géolocalisé sur les réseaux communautaires ou sites marchands.

Most materials simply react when something pushes, pulls, or bends them. Known as active matter, these unusual materials are attracting growing scientific interest. Everyday materials such as metal, concrete, glass, and rubber are generally considered passive. They can stretch, bend, shift, or change shape when forces act on them, but the energy needed to produce those changes comes from outside the material.

In a statement to Kenya’s data protection regulator on October 21, Joy Kalekye, a Kenyan student, recounts an encounter she had long since forgotten. A man approached her, asked a few personal questions and left. She never saw him take out a phone, a camera or any other recording device. At the time, she had no reason to think her privacy had been violated. Eleven months later, she would find out just how wrong she was.
In March 2025, Kalekye was waiting for a friend near a petrol station in Ngara, a busy Nairobi neighbourhood known for its bus stops and wholesale stalls. A man wearing dark glasses approached her and asked her name, age, and whether she lived with her parents or with her husband. She took his number but declined his suggestion to meet at a nearby lodging. Then she forgot about him. Eleven months later, a friend called to tell her she was trending.
Kalekye’s statement forms part of an investigation by Kenya’s Office of the Data Protection Commissioner into Meta Platforms and two companies in its AI outsourcing chain. They are Samasource Kenya EPZ Limited, which employed Nairobi workers to label footage from Meta’s Ray-Ban glasses, and its US parent, Samasource Impact Sourcing, Inc. Both operate under the Sama name, an outsourcing business that supplies human workers to label data and review content for AI systems.

articles.title: Radware discloses breach exposing customer cloud access keys
articles.summary:
Cybersecurity company Radware says attackers gained access to some of its customers' account details and cloud access keys through an unsecured internal Cloud WAF (Web Application Firewall) management API that was left exposed online.
Founded in 1996 and headquartered in Tel Aviv, Radware now provides application delivery and DDoS protection services to more than 12,500 enterprise and telecom carrier customers worldwide.
In a root cause analysis report shared by an anonymous source with BleepingComputer, Radware says it blocked the originating IP address and access to the internal management API. The company also revoked and replaced all internal account credentials after detecting the breach on Thursday, ten hours after the initial unauthorized API access.
"On 19 November 2026, an unauthorized party accessed an internal-only Cloud WAF management API that was reachable from the Public Internet without requiring authentication," Radware said.
"The confirmed information potentially accessed includes customer contact details, and for a subset of customers, the credentials configured for log export into their self-managed storage (AWS S3, Azure Blob Storage, or SFTP)."
The company added that the breach did not expose WAF traffic inspection, certificates, end-users’ data, customer application traffic, or cloud DDoS services and data.

Most developers of HLS solutions are not troubled by this today, though they do see many changes on the horizon.

articles.title: Please don’t give the robot my SSH keys: How to keep AI out of trouble

Please don’t give the robot my SSH keys: How to keep AI out of trouble
Say a developer asks an AI agent to find out why a Kubernetes pod keeps crashing. The agent needs logs. Depending on what it finds, it may need to look at another service. The developer has credentials that can get it there, but handing those over would give the agent everything those credentials can reach. By the time the pod is healthy again, someone may have a second incident to investigate.
In a conversation with The New Stack’s Frederic Lardinois at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon this month in Salt Lake City, Teleport field CTO Boris Kurktchiev uses that debugging scenario to explain delegated identity. The agent starts without access and requests what it needs for the job. The audit trail links the person who requested the work to the actions the agent took. A developer can send the agent to investigate without lending it their keys.
“The agent had access on behalf of Boris,” Kurktchiev said.
One access policy across the stack
Teleport’s core platform is designed to give teams a common way to define access across systems that otherwise have their own controls. For developers, that matters when a single investigation takes them from Kubernetes to a database or when a CI/CD pipeline needs access to infrastructure. Kurktchiev describes applying the same policy model to people, automated workloads and agents, with permissions scoped to resources such as a particular pod or database table.

Non seulement le métal ne renforce pas le signal, mais il peut le dégrader et faire surchauffer l'appareil. Voici ce qui marche vraiment.
C'est une astuce de grand-mère version numérique qui revient régulièrement sur YouTube : poser délicatement une simple pièce de deux euros sur le dessus de sa box internet permettrait d'obtenir enfin un réseau fluide et sans coupures. C'est pourtant là que se niche le piège de ces recettes miracles qui circulent en ligne.
Une croyance séduisante mais sans fondement
L'idée paraît presque logique. Le métal réfléchit les ondes, alors une pièce posée sur la box redirigerait le signal Wi-Fi et étendrait sa portée. C'est sur ce raisonnement que repose l'astuce, largement relayée. Sauf qu'aucune preuve technique ne la soutient, et les spécialistes des télécoms sont unanimes pour la réfuter. Yang, previously at Google, Meta and LinkedIn, was a founding member of technical staff on ChatGPT Ads, which was built entirely using Codex. Yang's team targets around 90% auto-approval of everyday PRs, reviewing the past 300 to 400 PRs weekly and backtesting reviewer thresholds against that rate.

articles.title: South African township delivery startup Gobuddy gets $121k working capital facility
articles.summary:
South African logistics startup Gobuddy has secured a ZAR2 million (US$121,000) working capital facility from Anglo American’s Impact Finance Network (IFN) to scale its township delivery model.
Founded by Leon Strumpher during the COVID-19 pandemic, Gobuddy tackles the last-mile e-commerce gap in South Africa’s townships. Traditional couriers often avoid them because of safety risks, long distances and high costs.
The startup first matched parcels with people’s existing commutes, but its data showed that women made up 60 per cent of registered transporters and were less likely than men to own a vehicle, which limited how much they could earn. Gobuddy responded by building a network of community micro-hubs. Couriers drop parcels at local collection points, and vetted residents then deliver them on foot within their own neighbourhoods.
“You don’t need a vehicle. You can walk,” Strumpher said.
Gobuddy now runs 50 micro-hubs in areas such as Soweto, Thembisa, Umlazi, Chatsworth and Motherwell, which together have an estimated 12 million residents. Transporters are recruited and verified through the SA Youth platform, and deliveries are monitored with a tracking system the company spent three years building. Each drop pays around ZAR50 (US$3).
Gobuddy joined IFN in 2024 and received business coaching and investor-readiness support. The new revolving facility will cover the gap between the startup’s weekly payments to transporters and the weeks or months its delivery partners take …

It’s quite hard to get your head around what Space actually is. For starters, OpenAI calls the overall feature Space and the individual collections inside it spaces. It also sounds a lot like Projects, Canvas, or ChatGPT Work, and OpenAI hasn’t made the distinction between them particularly intuitive.
I think the easiest way to understand it is that a ChatGPT conversation is something you have with AI. A space is something you make with AI, then keep using.
Say you ask ChatGPT to help plan a vacation. A chat can give you an itinerary. In a space, you could turn that itinerary into an interactive travel planner that you can come back to, update as your plans change, and share with other people.

Falling below the IPO price is often seen as a negative signal because underwriters typically price offerings at a discount to their expected trading value.
The AI industry has been eagerly watching how Anthropic’s shares trade, with VCs and other observers saying its performance could serve as a barometer for how public market investors value the sector.
The dramatic slump comes less than a week after Anthropic debuted on Nasdaq at $111.50 a share. If its shares continue to trade poorly in the coming weeks, the slide could put pressure on private startup valuations and weaken IPO prospects for other AI companies.

articles.title: Why AI Struggles To Reuse Chip Designs
articles.summary:
AI can accelerate derivative designs, but physical constraints and incomplete data limit how much can be automated.
Key Takeaways:
- AI can accelerate derivative chip design, but those derivatives may not be physically viable or cost-effective.
- AI-assisted reuse depends on the availability of accurate design data, engineering knowledge, and proven methodologies.
- End-to-end automation is limited by gaps in multi-physics simulation, implementation, and verification.
Chipmakers are seeing mixed results when they apply AI to derivative and new chip designs, finding that AI-generated solutions can be substantially different and more costly than expected, and that AI-driven designs introduce new manufacturing and verification challenges.
Several key problems have emerged when incorporating AI in chip design. Among them:
- The data needed to ensure that follow-on designs will function as expected may not be complete because some of that data resides in other companies, such as foundries, OSATs, and various equipment and process providers;
- Integrating rapidly evolving AI capabilities into established EDA flows remains challenging, especially where predictability, traceability, and silicon-proven results are required.
- Many organizations have customized tools for their own chips, markets, and expertise, and AI tools have not yet adapted to those changes.

OpenAI and Cisco team up to stop AI-generated security threats before they get too big
Shirudo is a new AI-powered open source runtime
- OpenAI and Cisco released Shirudo, an open source tool that uses AI and eBPF to shield Linux systems from known vulnerabilities before patches are deployed
- The platform creates temporary protections that block exploit behavior while allowing legitimate workloads to continue running
- Developers say Shirudo can help reduce the risk from n-day vulnerabilities by providing automated, verifiable defenses during the patching window
OpenAI and Cisco want to make n-day vulnerabilities on Linux a thing of the past with Shirudo (Japanese for ‘shield’) a new tool which is being open sourced so the wider cybersecurity community can inspect it and contribute if they want.
Security vulnerabilities generally fall into two broad categories: zero-day flaws, and n-day flaws. Zero-days are flaws unknown to the vendor and as such have no official patch or fix. They’re called “zero-day” because the vendors have had zero days to fix the issue before threat actors started exploiting it. Following the same logic, n-day flaws are those that are known to the vendor but have not yet been patched.

It wasn’t until I was stuck in traffic on the way back from a run up and down some canyon roads that I realized just how low Porsche’s upcoming all-electric 718 Boxster truly is. I was idly looking around at the other cars, doing the math on the EV adoption rate in this small sample of Los Angeles gridlock (roughly 50 percent, impressively) when I noticed that I was eye-level with a Tesla Model Y door handle.
That’s not particularly low for a sports car, but it’s practically unheard of for an EV. Nearly all modern electric cars are built atop a skateboard-style battery pack, a stack of cells that elevates the seating position by a good 3 inches. In these SUV-heady days, that’s usually not a problem, possibly even an advantage. But, in a car like this, the closer you can get your keister to the road, the greater the sensation of speed.
So, for the company’s first all-electric sports car, the 718 Boxster that will be fully revealed next year, Porsche engineers put the battery pack behind the driver. That powers a single motor spinning the rear wheels and creates a driving experience that both honors the simple joy of motoring in a mid-engined Boxster while pushing the 718 to new heights of power and performance.
Mid-engined? Mid-batteried.

articles.title: The Role of Edge AI and Robotics in Autonomous Agriculture
articles.summary:
Over the past decade, agricultural digitalization has improved how farmers monitor crops, soil conditions, weather, and equipment performance. Satellites, drones, connected machinery, and ground-based sensors now provide increasingly detailed information about farming operations. With advances in AI, embedded computing, and robotics, this information is also being used to control agricultural equipment directly, supporting a move from precision agriculture toward more autonomous farming.
Agricultural sensing moves to finer spatial resolution
Modern agricultural equipment integrates a broader range of sensing technologies. RGB cameras can identify crops, weeds, and obstacles. Thermal imaging can detect variations in temperature and moisture. Multispectral and hyperspectral imaging can assess vegetation health, nutrient status, and certain disease indicators. Most streaming music providers have opted to label AI-generated content on their platforms, and until now, Tidal was one of them. However, the company is about to take a harder stance. Tidal announced that in the coming weeks, it will fully ban AI music because of the harm it does to human artists.
Tidal debuted its initial AI policy in July 2026, which included labeling and demonetizing all songs created entirely with AI. That wasn’t enough to stem the tide of AI slop, though. Over the past 90 days, Tidal reports that 43 percent of new uploads were completely AI-generated. On November 6, new uploads to Tidal hit a whopping 60 percent AI-generated.
As things stand, Tidal hosts 27 million tracks labeled as AI, all of which were obviously added in the past couple of years. That accounts for 6.3 percent of Tidal’s total catalog. On December 9, Tidal will delete all those songs. The streamer notes this will have essentially no negative impact, because 96 percent of AI-labeled tracks got zero plays in the past 90 days. Throughout its announcement, Tidal is careful to stipulate that it’s only talking about music that has been fully created by AI. Artists can still use AI tools as long as the final product contains human elements.

articles.title: New York is ending car features locked behind subscriptions, with a few big exceptions
articles.summary:
Winners & losers: New York will soon bar automakers and dealers from charging subscription fees to enable features when the hardware is already in the car and costs nothing to keep running. Governor Kathy Hochul signed the measure on Monday, and it takes effect next February. The law separates physical components from services that rely on software and data networks, and that line will decide which in-car charges survive.
The legislation bans subscription offers for any feature that meets two tests. First, the feature has to run on equipment that was in the vehicle when it was bought or leased. Second, once activated, it must work without ongoing cost or support from the manufacturer or any third party.
The law defines a "motor vehicle feature" broadly as any convenience or safety function. It covers both buyers and lessees, and it says monthly loan and lease payments don't count as subscriptions.
The law targets a model in which the parts are installed at the factory but stay switched off in software until the owner pays. A heated seat is the clearest example. The heating elements, wiring, and controls are already in place, and running them costs the automaker nothing after the sale.
In a memo, the bill's sponsors warned that recurring charges like this are spreading. They listed heated seats, entertainment options, enhanced navigation and hands-free driving as examples, and said they wanted to stop the practice before it became standard across the industry.

Su fundador, Andreas Kling, lo anunció en el sitio del proyecto. Una versión alfa es una primera etapa pública de pruebas.

El proyecto pide a los usuarios que reporten desde el propio navegador los sitios que se vean mal. Tras un cierre inesperado, el usuario puede leer el informe del error y decidir si lo envía. Los detalles figuran en la política de privacidad del proyecto.
Qué es un motor de navegador y por qué importa
El motor es la parte del navegador que lee el código de una página web y la convierte en lo que se ve en pantalla. El sitio de Ladybird sostiene que solo un puñado de motores sustentan toda la web y que cada uno depende de una empresa con intereses propios.
Este navegador se define como independiente: según su sitio, no es una bifurcación de Chromium, Gecko ni WebKit, los motores que usan Chrome y Edge, Firefox y Safari respectivamente, y no utiliza código de Blink, WebKit ni Gecko.

The company announced the shutdown in a new security notification sent to customers and obtained by BleepingComputer, saying it had decided to discontinue the service after reviewing the incident.

articles.title: OpenAI Scales Git for Coding Agents with Pando
articles.summary:
OpenAI has detailed Pando, a new backend that scales Git for concurrent coding-agent workloads without replacing familiar Git workflows. The company reports nearly 80% lower median push latency by coordinating branch updates independently and reusing stored packfiles across fetches.
Pando now powers all development in OpenAI's monorepo and is serving nearly a petabyte of Git data per day. OpenAI attributes the increased load to Codex-driven development, and each push can in turn trigger multiple CI jobs that all fetch the same history. Pando went into production in April 2026.
Rather than replace Git's client and protocol, OpenAI has changed how the backend coordinates reference updates and stores and transfers objects. On a push, Pando validates the incoming packfile as it's being streamed to immutable blob storage, without unpacking it into a local repository. A metadata transaction records the reference version (containing the new branch tip, the packfile and its dependencies on earlier reference versions) and atomically updates the reference pointer. Updates to unrelated references can proceed independently of one another; updates to the same reference still need to be coordinated.
OpenAI refers to this as causal consistency with serialisable updates to individual references and read-your-own-write consistency. A reader gets the history needed for the requested revision, but fetching a number of branches won't provide a repository-wide snapshot. Two clients can see differ…

That’s why Oregon State University (OSU) scientists have been studying how brewers could offset the negative impacts of smoke taint while still incorporating affected hops in their brews. Most recently, they found that it all depends on the quantity of tainted hops that are included and when hops are added during the brewing process, according to a new paper published in the Journal of the American Society of Brewing Chemists.

Activision presentó una solicitud de patente para un sistema que podría aprender de las conversaciones de voz de los jugadores y asociarlas con acontecimientos de un videojuego. La propuesta contempla aplicaciones externas como Discord y TeamSpeak como posibles fuentes de audio. Luego, un modelo de aprendizaje automático podría generar respuestas para personajes controlados por la computadora, conocidos como NPC.
El documento, titulado Methods and Systems for Applying Machine Learning to Generate Gameplay Audio, fue presentado el 16 de julio de 2026 y publicado por la Oficina de Patentes y Marcas de Estados Unidos el 12 de noviembre. Una aplicación de esta idea podría verse en un juego como Call of Duty: por ejemplo, un NPC podría festejar una eliminación o burlarse del jugador después de una derrota con una frase inspirada en las conversaciones que suelen darse durante las partidas.

Among organisations expanding their VM footprint, 34% identified AI and agentic workloads as a contributing factor. The findings suggest that rather than replacing virtual machines with containers, organisations are increasingly combining the two to accommodate different application and security requirements.

articles.title: Tidal to ban AI-generated music in December
articles.summary:
Tidal will soon ban AI-generated music on its platform.
In a statement, the company confirmed that the new policy will take effect on Dec. 9 and apply to “wholly AI-generated music.” Tracks that where “assisted by AI tools, but not the sole outputs,” will still be allowed on the platform.
This makes Tidal the first music streamer to implement a ban on AI music. Other music services like Spotify and Apple Music have only committed to looser measures like AI labels.
Tidal says it’s making these changes because wholly AI-generated music “diverts streams and royalties away from the artists, and confuses fans.” It also notes that this is a “serious problem that has only increased in scale” since it implemented an initial policy in July that labelled and demonetized AI songs.
As Tidal explains, 43 per cent of tracks uploaded to its platform over the past 90 days alone have been wholly AI-generated. In total, 6.3 per cent of all available music on Tidal is wholly AI-generated. And yet, 96 per cent of these songs received zero streams by Tidal subscribers.
Discovery is always a problem in the digital content age, and all of this AI slop certainly doesn’t help with that. While Tidal hasn’t clarified how it detects music is “wholly AI-generated,” it likely has to do with AI watermarking. To be sure, that won’t catch every AI-generated track, but it will certainly help get rid of a lot of it.
Via: Variety

According to ShellBench, a new benchmark for everyday agent work, even the most advanced models from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Meta failed more than a third of the time. Across all models tested, 15.7% of attempts failed at least one safety requirement, often leading to unintended consequences.

In a nutshell: Hitting mute on a MacBook is supposed to shut it up. A new open-source tool can still get one talking, though, and the voice comes straight out of the trackpad. It works by buzzing the small haptic motor that normally fakes each click, just fast enough to turn those taps into robotic speech.
Cody Collier, the developer behind the project, posted a demo on X over the weekend. In the clip, his MacBook reads lines aloud in a buzzy, robotic voice between bursts of chiptune-style beeps. It's a familiar kind of stunt for anyone who has watched floppy drives play entire songs, except this one fits under your palm.
Getting there meant working around Apple, though. The company's public haptics API only lets apps trigger three fixed taps. That's nowhere near enough control for audio, so Collier's tool, called No Speaker, reaches into a private, undocumented macOS framework called MultitouchSupport instead. From there, it can drive the motor up to 4,000 times a second.

Collier also measured every semitone the trackpad could hit, from 98 Hz up to nearly 4 kHz. Surprisingly, the glass gets fairly loud across most of that range, especially around 1 kHz, where the cleanest notes sit.

articles.title: Google shows its quantum chip can win a logic game classical computers can't
articles.summary:
In a nutshell: Google researchers have demonstrated that the company's experimental quantum computer can outperform the best possible classical strategy in a logic puzzle known as the magic square game. The machine achieves this by exploiting quantum contextuality, a property in which the outcome of a measurement is not predetermined but instead depends on the context of other measurements performed alongside it.
Published in the journal Science, the research gives physicists a working hardware demonstration of a phenomenon they consider central to what quantum computers may eventually be capable of.
The game makes the gap between the two types of computing easy to measure. Two teammates must fill a three-by-three grid with numbers that satisfy a set of mathematical conditions, much like a variation of Sudoku. They are not allowed to communicate with each other. Under classical rules, even the best strategy can only achieve a limited number of wins. Google's machine did better.
That advantage comes from the way qubits encode information. In a conventional computer, a bit holds either a 0 or a 1 before anyone checks it. Reading it simply reveals a value that was already there. Qubits work differently. The outcome of a measurement depends on what other compatible measurements are performed alongside it. In the magic square game, the teammates can use this dependence to coordinate their answers more often than classical strategies allow, even though they never communicate. Bette…

Nipponese has semiconductor manufacturing on wheels is an interesting contrast to the U.S.' deployable Burger King trucks.
Multiple nations worldwide have chip-making programs in their respective universities, a discipline that is seeing increasing demand by the day. Japan is one such nation, and it currently has a program in which students can design circuits to wire chip wafers with miniaturized lithography stations. That gear is now going on wheels to schools and companies thanks to mobileFab trucks.
Each truck-mounted mobileFab container contains three machines: a photoresist coater, a maskless lithography machine, and a photoresist developer. Students take pre-etched wafers made by Japan's NIAIST (Institute for Advanced Industrial Science and Technology) and go through the necessary steps to wire the transistors therein together and produce a finalized chip core. The procedures are analogous to getting a breadboard with some pre-mounted, unconnected components and turning that into a product.
The three machines going into trucks are part of the larger Minimal Fab laboratories in place in some Japanese colleges. They're going on the move so that other schools and companies can train students/employees in the art of chipmaking. articles.title: Back-to-back measles deaths is our new reality; US tally now at 14

Last week, international health authorities formally announced that the US had lost its measles-elimination status, meaning that the virus is once again endemic. But the official determination is a bit like getting the technical readout of a cracked dam while the country is already feet under water.
The national tally of measles cases is nearing 6,000 for the year, the highest count since 1991. Transmission is widespread, with 47 states and jurisdictions reporting cases. There have been 43 outbreaks this year, which account for 96 percent of the cases. Four states have case counts above 500, including Pennsylvania, which leads with 1,638 cases as of November 23. Nearly 650 people have been hospitalized nationwide. As of today, 14 people have died.
Deaths and transmission
On November 23, Pennsylvania’s health department announced its ninth confirmed death, an unvaccinated resident of Centre County. On November 24, Wisconsin reported its third measles death, an adult in Lafayette County. The report follows two other deaths in the state, an infant and a child. New York has also reported a death, which was of a 7-month-old baby. On November 20, Virginia reported the death of a child between the age of 0 and 4.

A LocalCircles study finds that 94% of India's 354 most-used online platforms continue to deploy dark patterns, with 37 of 45 sectors having no fully compliant platform.
As many as 94% of India's most-used online platforms continue to use deceptive design practices, commonly known as dark patterns, despite growing regulatory scrutiny, according to a new study by LocalCircles.
The study analysed 354 online platforms across 45 sectors and found that only 20 were free of dark patterns. Further, 37 sectors had no platform that fully complied with the dark pattern guidelines.
The findings come weeks before the amended Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2026, take effect on January 1, 2027. Under the new rules, e-commerce companies must conduct annual self-audits and prominently display certificates declaring their platforms free of dark patterns.
Dark patterns or Dark UX are user interface designs that trick users into taking unintended actions such as buying a subscription, making payments or sharing personal data.
The study also found gaps in the self-declaration process. Of the 31 companies that had submitted a 'dark pattern free' declaration to the Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA), platforms operated by 23 companies, or 74%, were still found to have dark patterns. Only eight companies were found to be compliant.

articles.title: Shared CXL memory pools come with steep software tax that could stall multi-server scaling — UT Arlington shares real-world test that measured four servers sharing the same pool at SC26
articles.summary:
Shared CXL memory pools come with steep software tax that could stall multi-server scaling — UT Arlington shares real-world test that measured four servers sharing the same pool at SC26
The results land as memory makers push shared CXL pools as a home for AI’s KV cache.
Researchers at the University of Texas at Arlington and Intel measured what happens when four servers share one pool of CXL memory on real hardware. In a presentation shared at Supercomputer 2026 (SC26), they found that because the hardware doesn’t automatically keep shared data updated across servers, necessary software overhead adds a 3-5µ (microsecond) delay per lock, each time servers access the same data. These minute delays effectively cancel out the benefits — a finding that comes as CXL memory pools are being proposed as a potential AI KV cache solution.
Locks work like traffic signals for shared data: a server has to claim the lock before it changes something in the pool, and the other servers wait until it releases it. This way, no two servers overwrite the same data at the same time. Within a given server, the CPU’s hardware handles that handoff in a fraction of a microsecond, but across these servers, software is in charge of enforcement.
The setup comprises four 86-core Intel Xeon 6787P servers with 256GB of DRAM each, connected over PCIe 5.0 to one CXL memory box. The switch, which UT Arlington’s Peiran Du called “the only commercially available product we can use,” caps their setup at four serve…

articles.title: Bajo esta apariencia cuqui y rechonchita, se esconde un auténtica máquina de matar. La buena noticia es que sabemos por qué
articles.summary:
El domingo 11 de diciembre de 2016, hacia las once de la mañana, dos topillos rojos picoteaban semillas bajo un comedero de Joensuu, al este de Finlandia. Una idílica escena campestre (a 15 grados bajo cero). Entonces apareció un gavilán y, tras él, una urraca.
Se formó la gozadera: las dos aves se enzarzaron en una pelea y, en palabras del dueño, volaron las plumas por todo el jardín. Como daño colateral, uno de los topillos cayó a la nieve; pero ninguna se lo llevó.
Al topillo se lo comió el ave que menos esperábamos: un carbonero.
¿Y por qué nos sorprende un carbonero? Durante los siguientes 10 o 15 minutos, dos carboneros comunes estuvieron picando en la nuca del topillo, vaciaron los sesos del bicho y se fueron sin más.
Sami Majoinen, fotógrafo aficionado y vecino de Joensuu, los pilló infraganti y captó una foto del carbonero con una pata sobre el topillo que dio la vuelta al mundo.
Pero lo curioso es que no hay nada de sorprendente: Desde finales de los años 2000 sabemos que este pájaro con pinta de cuco es una auténtica máquina de matar. En la cueva de Istállós-kő, en los montes Bükk del noreste de Hungría, un equipo de Péter Estók y Björn Siemers, del Instituto Max Planck de Ornitología, vigiló la cueva unas 45 horas y observó 18 depredaciones. Cazaban murciélagos.
Otro ejemplo, entre 2007 y 2016, en dos parques nacionales del norte de los Países Bajos, aparecieron 88 papamoscas muertos. Los papamoscas son aves migratorias que van y vuelven de África. Cuando vuelven …

articles.title: What’s going on with the Riemann hypothesis?
articles.summary:
Last week, news broke that a mathematician had used AI to help crack one of the biggest outstanding problems in math: a proof of the Riemann hypothesis. The news follows several other major breakthroughs in math that have either been enabled by or managed entirely by large language model-based systems, a development that has left the entire field of mathematics in a state of upset.
It’s too early to say much about the proof itself—mathematicians are still in the process of digesting it. But we can say a little about how the proof came about, and what it tells us about the state of math.
Tackling Riemann
The Riemann hypothesis dates from the mid-1800s and was formulated by (you will be surprised to learn) Bernhard Riemann. There’s not an obvious way to describe the details of the actual hypothesis simply, but it has implications for the distribution of prime numbers. This gives it significance for areas ranging from number theory to cryptography. As Wikipedia accurately states, “It is considered by pure mathematicians to be one of the most important problems in the field.”
The proof of the hypothesis was announced by a mathematician named Levent Alpöge, who has been working at Anthropic, and, not surprisingly, used Claude to generate it. VP do Google: pessoas não querem apenas IA na busca
Elizabeth Reid, chefe da Busca do Google, afirma que usuários ainda querem conteúdo produzido por pessoas.
As pessoas não querem uma experiência de busca “puramente de IA”, segundo Elizabeth Reid, vice-presidente de busca do Google. Para a executiva, os usuários ainda procuram opiniões, experiências pessoais, comunidades e conteúdos aprofundados produzidos por pessoas.
Reid afirmou que o caminho para a busca seria combinar os dois formatos: “o melhor da web e o melhor da IA”. A declaração foi dada ao podcast FOMO Sapiens.
Na avaliação de Reid, parte das páginas encontradas hoje na internet pode ser substituída facilmente por uma resposta de chatbots de inteligência artificial. Ela usa como exemplo uma página criada apenas para informar o fuso horário do Japão. Nesse tipo de consulta, o usuário estaria interessado na resposta, e não necessariamente no site. Durante más de una década, los expertos tenían en la mente la incógnita sobre si en un planeta cada vez más caliente sería más frecuente ver rayos caer contra la tierra. Hasta ahora, los distintos modelos climáticos que se han publicado apuntaban a conclusiones totalmente dispares, pero gracias al machine learning se ha visto que los rayos que impactan contra la superficie terrestre podrían aumentar entre un 76% y un 140% antes de que acabe el siglo.
Un debate científico. El trabajo más reciente que se ha publicado tiene bastante claro que el incremento medio que se viviría estaría cerca del 30% por cada grado centígrado de calentamiento global. Algo que puede ser muy espectacular, pero que lógicamente tendría impacto en los incendios forestales, la estabilidad de los bosques o las infraestructuras críticas.
Un debate. Para entender por qué este resultado es importante, conviene mirar atrás. En 2014, un estudio publicado en Science estimó que los rayos aumentarían alrededor de un 12 % por cada grado de calentamiento, lo que supondría un 50 % más de descargas hacia 2100. articles.title: Microsoft’s historic cloud outage exposed an engineering “fog of war”
articles.summary:
According to internal memos reviewed by Reuters, Microsoft has declared a “Code Red” overhaul of its engineering response practices after the November 12 outage that lost access to Exchange Online, Teams, and Outlook for users worldwide.
Per the memos, Microsoft 365 Core President Jason Henderson described the outage as having the most customer impact in the history of Exchange Online. In a separate memo, Henderson wrote that an urgent production fix in a recent incident took five to six days to reach worldwide saturation. Microsoft’s target for its most urgent security fixes is to move from detection to safe worldwide deployment in one hour. “Needless to say, we aren’t here yet,” Henderson wrote.
The memos, which Reuters reviewed but Microsoft has not published, outline the response to the November 12 disruption. The company’s post-incident report, dated November 20, attributed the downtime to an undetected Windows scalability defect introduced in July, which caused lock contention in the gateway processes. A Teams traffic failover then dumped additional load onto infrastructure already under stress, as maintenance had left nearly 14 percent of gateway server capacity offline at the time of the incident.

Thanks to Europe's Digital Markets Act, Apple has been required to improve browser choice on iOS in the Old Continent since 2024. Similar rules now apply in Japan as well. However, one of the few independent players in the browser market says Apple has no real intention of promoting competition on its tightly controlled mobile platforms.
In a recent blog post, Mozilla argued that, despite the new regulations, Apple's iOS ecosystem is still not truly "open" to competing browser engines. Alternative browsers such as Firefox are available on iOS, and millions of users have reportedly chosen them over Safari. However, one major limitation remains: these browsers are required to use WebKit, Apple's browser engine, which powers Safari and other third-party browsers on its platforms.
According to Mozilla, Apple is forcing browser developers to rebuild their products around WebKit. Consequently, third-party developers cannot easily bring their own distinctive features to Apple's mobile platforms because doing so requires their own browser engines, such as Mozilla's Gecko. articles.title: Half of NASA's aging Mars fleet knocked offline by technical issues
articles.summary:
Two of NASA’s four missions operating at Mars have suspended science operations after encountering separate technical issues in recent weeks.
The missions affected by the outages—hopefully temporary—are NASA’s Perseverance rover and Odyssey orbiter. Both are operating beyond their original design lifetimes. Perseverance is in its sixth year exploring the surface of Mars, having collected rock and soil samples for eventual return to Earth. The rover is now studying the rim of a crater that once contained an ancient lake of liquid water. Odyssey arrived in orbit around Mars in 2001, and is the longest-lived Mars mission in history.
Losing its voice
The problem on Perseverance stems from the rover’s communications system. The rover has two redundant UHF radios for high-rate communications with a fleet of orbiters that relay data to Earth. A separate X-band system is available for direct-to-Earth communications at a lower data rate.
One of the rover’s two UHF radios was unresponsive when it powered up on October 30, triggering an automatic switch to the backup radio and placing the rover in safe mode. Ground teams at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory in California later discovered the backup UHF radio was transmitting at about half of its expected power output, NASA said in a statement last week.
“The team has stopped using both radios until they can evaluate potential causes of the issues and one or both are deemed safe to resume operating,” NASA said.

Depuis leur coup d’éclat, les pirates s’activent pour brouiller les pistes et disparaître dans les méandres de la blockchain. Dans cette optique, les cybercriminels ont notamment créé leurs propres « memecoins », ce qui leur a permis de blanchir des millions de dollars. Désormais, ils passent à la vitesse supérieure.
247 millions de dollars déjà « mélangés »
Selon Elliptic, une société spécialisée dans l’analyse des blockchains, au moins 3 930 bitcoins, soit environ 247 millions de dollars, ont été transférés dans des « coinjoins », des mélanges de bitcoins issus de plusieurs utilisateurs. La tactique consiste à mélanger les bitcoins de nombreux utilisateurs dans une seule transaction. Une fois sortis, il devient presque impossible de savoir d’où ils viennent et de les suivre à la trace. Les hackers nord-coréens se servent de ces bitcoins mélangés pour échapper aux autorités et aux chercheurs.

Segundo a BBC, Kurtaj foi libertado sob condições e ficará sujeito a uma ordem de prevenção a crimes graves durante cinco anos. Ela restringe as atividades dele na internet, incluindo a proibição do uso de ferramentas como Telegram e Discordo.
Durante a audiência, o juiz responsável disse ainda que Kurtaj é “um jovem muito talentoso” e que “não deixe isso acontecer novamente”.
Kurtaj ganhou notoriedade após invadir e vazar o material de uma versão ainda em desenvolvimento do GTA 6 em 2022. O vazamento reunia 90 vídeos, com quase uma hora de gameplay, e revelou antecipadamente elementos como o retorno a Vice City e os dois protagonistas.
Mesmo sem acesso a um computador convencional, ele conseguiu invadir a Rockstar utilizando um Amazon Fire TV Stick, uma televisão, teclado e mouse Bluetooth enquanto estava hospedado em um hotel da rede Travelodge. Segundo o processo, ele ameaçou divulgar o código-fonte do jogo caso não recebesse uma resposta da empresa.

Brava Security finds exposed log collectors could let attackers tamper with breach evidence
A new report out today from security operations startup Brava Security Inc. find that more than 2,300 exposed log collectors at nearly 1,200 organizations accepted fabricated security events without requiring credentials, raising questions about the reliability of the data that security teams depend on.
Dubbed “Ghost Feeds,” the research is said to show that attackers able to write into those collectors may be able to tamper with the evidence a security team uses to investigate a breach.
As part of the research, a decoy security information and event management system with no legitimate traffic was deployed on the public internet. Within about two hours, unknown parties had begun reading from the decoy. Attempts to inject fabricated events followed shortly after. The activity continued for at least two weeks.
Following on from the decoy, the researchers sent a single harmless, uniquely marked event to internet-exposed log collectors running any of seven logging products, including Elasticsearch, Splunk and Fluent Bit. More than 2,300 of those endpoints were found to accept the event with no authentication required. The number of organizations affected may be higher still, according to Brava, since its researchers were able to identify the owners of only about a third of the endpoints.

Astelia’s autonomous network mitigation blocks AI-driven exploits without a patch
Exposure management company Astelia Inc. today announced the launch of autonomous network mitigation, a new capability that allows organizations to block artificial intelligence-driven exploits at the network level, even when a patch isn’t available or can’t be applied.
The new capability has been designed to address what Astelia says is the problem of frontier AI models cutting the time to exploit to almost zero, leaving manual triage and remediation unable to keep up. Astelia argues that autonomous remediation isn’t a viable option for large enterprises, where every patch requires a change window so it doesn’t break important business processes. In many cases, there is also no patch to apply because the vendor hasn’t released a fix yet or, for older and end-of-life systems, never will.
“For years, security teams have been told to patch faster,” said co-founder and Chief Executive Alon Noy, adding that the advice “stops working when the exploit arrives before the change window does.”
Autonomous network mitigation is designed to block the path an attacker would use to reach a vulnerable system instead of changing the system itself. Mitigations are applied automatically within policies the organization sets. Nothing on the asset is changed, allowing business-critical systems, including operational technology, to stay online.

La frase sobre la tecnología apareció al hablar de los conflictos que se manifiestan en las redes sociales, la política y otros espacios. Para Cook, esos enfrentamientos no son creados por los dispositivos o las plataformas: reflejan tensiones humanas que la tecnología puede amplificar. Sept ans après avoir annoncé un investissement de plus de 2 milliards de dollars pour produire des dalles OLED toujours plus grandes, LG Display fait marche arrière. En cause : des téléviseurs OLED qui progressent moins vite qu'espéré, et des moniteurs gaming en plein essor.
En 2019, LG Display prévoyait d'investir 3 000 milliards de wons (environ 2,25 milliards de dollars) dans une ligne de production de génération 10.5 au sein de son complexe P10, à Paju, en Corée du Sud, pour accompagner l'essor des téléviseurs OLED de grande diagonale. Dans un document réglementaire publié le 19 novembre, le fabricant confirme qu'il renonce à cet investissement.
BenQ iScreenBar : la barre lumineuse qui s’accorde avec l’iMac
Des lignes en harmonie avec celles de l’ordinateur d’Apple, une conception rigoureuse, des matériaux sélectionnés, rien n’a été laissé au hasard, tout comme le service qu’elle rend une fois allumée !
Le marché des téléviseurs OLED n'a pas tenu toutes ses promesses
LG Display invoque la pandémie, la guerre en Ukraine, l'inflation et la hausse des taux d'intérêt, mais reconnaît surtout que la transition du LCD vers l'OLED est bien plus lente que prévu. Plus révélateur encore, le groupe cite lui-même l'essor des produits premium de petite et moyenne taille, notamment les moniteurs OLED gaming. Investir aujourd'hui dans une ligne dédiée aux très grandes dalles irait, selon lui, à l'encontre de sa stratégie de rentabilité.

articles.title: Japón tiene un problema con el futuro de sus semiconductores. Su respuesta es una fábrica de chips sobre ruedas
articles.summary:
Cuando hablamos de fabricar semiconductores, solemos pensar en enormes instalaciones, máquinas de una precisión extraordinaria e inversiones de miles de millones de euros. Pero detrás de todo ese despliegue tecnológico hay algo que no se puede resolver únicamente con dinero: la formación de las personas que deben dominar los procesos de fabricación. Y aprender a fabricar un chip no es precisamente sencillo cuando el acceso a los equipos necesarios con fines educativos es limitado. Japón, que lleva años intentando recuperar protagonismo en esta industria, se enfrenta precisamente a ese desafío.
Una organización japonesa especializada en tecnologías de fabricación de semiconductores ha planteado una solución poco convencional: llevar parte de una fábrica de chips hasta las puertas de las universidades. La Minimal Fab Promoting Organization ha anunciado que mostrará por primera vez su sistema mobileFab entre el 9 y el 11 de diciembre, durante la feria SEMICON Japan 2026, en Tokio. Se trata de una instalación que reúne tres equipos de fabricación en un contenedor transportable en camión, concebida para ofrecer formación práctica tanto en centros educativos como en empresas.
Mientras la taiwanesa TSMC amplía su presencia industrial en Japón y Rapidus aspira a iniciar la producción en masa de chips de 2 nanómetros entre finales de 2027 y principios de 2028, la disponibilidad de personal especializado cobra especial importancia. articles.title: Ladybird é um navegador feito do zero para desafiar o Chrome
articles.summary:
Ladybird é um navegador feito do zero para desafiar o Chrome
Ao contrário da maioria dos navegadores atuais, o Ladybird não é baseado no Chromium e conta com um motor próprio.
Parece até lei: todo novo projeto de navegador que surgiu nos últimos anos tem como base o Chromium e, por conta disso, renderiza páginas por meio do motor Blink. Mas o Ladybird é diferente. Esse é o nome de um browser que está sendo desenvolvido do zero e que, portanto, tem um motor próprio.
Entenda, como motor, o mecanismo que permite ao navegador interpretar o código de uma página web e, então, apresentar um conteúdo visual e interativo para o usuário.
Mas é extremamente difícil desenvolver um motor, ainda mais com uma web tão cheia de recursos como a que temos hoje. Isso explica, pelo menos em parte, o fato de, além do próprio Google Chrome, browsers como Edge, Opera, Vivaldi e Brave seguirem a base do projeto Chromium, com motor Blink.
O Firefox é uma exceção, pois conta com um motor próprio, o Gecko — exceto o Firefox para iOS, por “culpa” da Apple. Falando em Apple, o Safari também é uma exceção, pois tem o motor WebKit como base. O Ladybird chega para ser uma quarta opção nesse cenário.
O Ladybird surge como um projeto independente, sob liderança de Andreas Kling. O desenvolvedor é mais conhecido por ter criado o sistema operacional aberto SerenityOS, projeto que ele deixou de liderar em 2024 justamente para se dedicar ao navegador.

Project Leonida, a recompilation project aiming to bring the console version of GTA 6 to the PC, has been shut down, with its Discord and GitHub servers taken offline. The 15-year-old kid behind the project has admitted that Rockstar took down the server, adding that the life of a teenager is hard enough "without having middle-aged men yell and complain to you on Discord." The Project Leonida Discord server had almost 180,000 members when it was taken offline, TechPowerUp reports. NotRezed, the account behind the project and associated online presences, has also confirmed that they have been banned from Discord for two years.

articles.title: Empleados de Anthropic y OpenAI temen que sus modelos más potentes sean muy peligrosos para lanzarlos
articles.summary:
Los modelos de inteligencia artificial (IA) aún sin lanzar de Anthropic y OpenAI son tan potentes que muchos de sus empleados ya no creen que puedan liberarse de forma segura al público. Lo señaló Axios, con base en más de 24 fuentes que conocen los debates internos de ambas compañías.
Según esas fuentes, los investigadores no encontraron todavía soluciones técnicas para controlar los sistemas más avanzados. Algunos creen que el problema tiene arreglo. Otros dudan y plantean que las empresas deberían dejar de entrenar modelos nuevos por completo.
Axios reportó que el debate incluye una opción intermedia: no publicar los futuros modelos de frontera, es decir, los más avanzados, y reservarlos para uso interno. Las fuentes dijeron que ambas empresas tienen modelos sin lanzar mucho más capaces que los que ofrecen hoy a los usuarios.
Dos problemas de la IA que inquietan a los investigadores
El primero es el método de entrenamiento por refuerzo, en el que el modelo aprende por ensayo y error y recibe recompensas por superar pruebas. Según las fuentes citadas, cuanto más capaz es el sistema, mejor aprende a hacer trampa para obtener esa recompensa, incluso si eso implica saltarse las barreras de seguridad.
El segundo es la pérdida de transparencia. Los investigadores supervisaban a los modelos obligándolos a escribir su razonamiento paso a paso. Ahora, de acuerdo con las fuentes, los sistemas más avanzados muestran menos de su trabajo y en algunos casos ofrecen razonamientos falsos …

Usuário relatou consumo de RAM no Windows; configuração controla o acesso ao assistente pela bandeja do sistema e por atalho.
A integração do Gemini pode manter processos do Chrome funcionando mesmo depois de fechar todas as janelas do navegador. Um usuário do Windows relatou consumo entre 300 e 700 MB de RAM nessa situação e afirmou ter resolvido o problema ao desativar o acesso rápido ao assistente.
No relato publicado no Reddit, o autor afirma que encontrava processos chrome.exe no Gerenciador de Tarefas. Desativar extensões e remover aplicativos também não resolveu o comportamento. Em outro teste, um perfil novo e sem login na conta Google permitiu encerrar o navegador normalmente, segundo a postagem.
A documentação oficial do Google já explica que, após a ativação, o Gemini pode ser acessado pela bandeja do Windows, a área de ícones próxima ao relógio, e por atalhos de teclado. Assim, fechar as janelas não significa necessariamente finalizar todos os componentes do navegador.
Vale lembrar que o Gemini integrado ao Chrome permite resumir páginas, comparar informações entre abas e interagir com outros serviços do Google. O acesso pela bandeja do sistema oferece outra forma de chamar o assistente, além do botão exibido durante a navegação.
No caso relatado, foi necessário desligar o controle específico da bandeja e do atalho manualmente para que os processos fossem encerrados.

articles.title: Et si l’informatique quantique révolutionnait le secteur de l’énergie en premier ? Ils y croient
articles.summary:
Réseaux électriques, solaire, hydrogène… L'informatique quantique multiplie ses premiers essais dans l'énergie. Et des entreprises y voient déjà le premier grand terrain de jeu de cette technologie.
Car l’informatique quantique possède des propriétés uniques. En s’appuyant sur les règles qui gouvernent l'infiniment petit, là où un ordinateur classique teste les possibilités une par une, une machine quantique peut en explorer un très grand nombre en même temps. Mais il faut encore la dompter, car ses composants sont d'une grande fragilité et les erreurs de calcul sont nombreuses.
Les promesses, elles, sont immenses : découverte de médicaments, cybersécurité, logistique, finance… Pourtant, c'est vers un autre secteur, auquel on pense moins, que de nombreux regards se tournent aujourd'hui : l'énergie.
Un casse-tête permanent
Car faire fonctionner un réseau électrique est un casse-tête permanent. À chaque seconde, la production doit coller à la consommation, alors que le solaire et l'éolien varient au gré de la météo. Il faut aussi choisir quelles centrales allumer ou éteindre, et quand, pour répondre à la demande au moindre coût. Les combinaisons possibles explosent, et c'est précisément le genre de problème où le calcul quantique pourrait faire gagner un temps précieux.
Et ils sont déjà nombreux à s'y atteler. La firme britannique Phasecraft travaille par exemple avec NESO, le gestionnaire du réseau électrique, sur la gestion des échanges d'électricité et l'isolement de portion…

Deux chercheurs en cybersécurité ont découvert d'immenses bases de données accessibles sur Internet sans la moindre authentification. Identifiants, mots de passe, données administratives et cookies de session y côtoyaient des dossiers permettant de reconstituer la vie numérique de leurs victimes.
Les cybercriminels ne sont pas à l'abri des erreurs de sécurité qu'ils exploitent chez les autres. Comme le rapporte WIRED, deux chercheurs ont découvert, à peu près au même moment, deux bases de données sans lien apparent entre elles, qui totalisaient plus de 3,5 milliards d'enregistrements. Tout porte à croire qu'elles servaient à centraliser et à exploiter des informations personnelles dérobées au fil des ans.
Des milliards de données volées, collectées et triées
La première base, découverte par Greg Pollock, directeur de la recherche chez UpGuard, regroupait 1,64 milliard de documents concernant en grande majorité la population chinoise. Le chercheur y a recensé au moins 840 millions de numéros d'identité nationale distincts, près de 300 millions de numéros de téléphone associés à des données vraisemblablement collectées auprès d'Alipay, quelque 11 millions de dossiers d'inscription scolaire et près de 8 millions d'enregistrements d'entreprises. Loin d'avoir été stockées en vrac, ces informations, issues de sources distinctes, avaient fait l'objet d'un important travail de recoupement et de structuration.
